summary: Let K/Q_p be finite and ρ an n-dimensional crystabelline representation of Gal_K with regular Hodge–Tate weights, generic and non-critical. Classical local Langlands together with the Hodge–Tate weights produces the locally algebraic representation π_alg(φ,h) = π_sm(φ) ⊗ L(λ) of GL_n(K), and for n ≥ 3 this loses the position of the Hodge filtration relative to the φ-stable flags — a positive-dimensional family of parameters, invisible on the automorphic side until now. The paper finds them. Working with (φ,Γ)-modules over the Robba ring, it reinterprets the Hodge parameter of D ∈ ΦΓ_nc(φ,h) as the map ι_D: D_1 ↪ D ↠ C_1 between the rank n-1 subobject and quotient, taken up to scalar, and shows that it determines D when K = Q_p (and that its σ-analogue always determines the modified module D_σ). On the GL_n(K)-side it builds, from the n! locally analytic principal series attached to the refinements, an amalgamated representation π_1(φ,h) depending only on (φ,h), computes Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) to be of dimension n + (2^n-1)d_K, and proves its central theorem (Theorem 3.21): the amalgamation of the trianguline deformation spaces of D factors through that extension group, giving a surjection t_D onto \bar{Ext}^1(D,D) whose kernel has dimension (2^n - n(n+1)/2 - 1)d_K. The kernel is the parameter: the extension π_min(D) of π_alg(φ,h) ⊗ Ker(t_D) by π_1(φ,h) satisfies π_min(D) ≅ π_min(D') iff D_σ ≅ D'_σ for every σ, so for K = Q_p it determines ρ (Theorem 3.34). Finally the paper proves that this is not an artefact: in the patched setting of Caraiani–Emerton–Gee–Geraghty–Paškūnas–Shin, and again in the completed cohomology of a definite unitary group under a vanishing hypothesis on the adjoint Selmer group, π_min(D) embeds in the p-adic automorphic representation attached to ρ and is the maximal subrepresentation of its shape (Theorem 4.5, Corollary 4.8, Theorem 4.18), so that Π_∞[m_ρ] determines ρ when K = Q_p. What the atlas lacks: everything. There is no roadmap for locally analytic representations of a p-adic reductive group (Orlik–Strauch functors, Emerton's Jacquet functor and adjunction, Schraen's spectral sequence); none for the trianguline variety or the deformation theory of trianguline (φ,Γ)-modules, which is why PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 proposes one and this paper feeds the same one; and none for the p-adic Langlands correspondence beyond GL_2(Q_p).

items.name: The local setting: K, E, the embeddings Σ_K and algebraic characters z^k
items.statement: K is a finite extension of Q_p and E a finite extension of Q_p containing every embedding of K into an algebraic closure; Σ_K is the set of embeddings σ: K ↪ E and d_K = [K:Q_p] = #Σ_K. For k = (k_σ)_{σ∈Σ_K} ∈ Z^{Σ_K}, z^k is the Q_p-algebraic character z ↦ ∏_{σ∈Σ_K} σ(z)^{k_σ} of K^×. |·|_K is the unramified character with |ϖ_K|_K = p^{-[K_0:Q_p]}; local class field theory is normalised by sending a uniformiser to a geometric Frobenius, so that the cyclotomic character ε, viewed as a character of K^×, equals N_{K/Q_p}(·)|·|_K.

items.name: Locally Q_p-analytic, smooth and locally σ-analytic characters of a locally K-analytic group
items.statement: For a locally K-analytic group H, Hom(H,E) is the E-vector space of locally Q_p-analytic E-valued characters, Hom_sm(H,E) the subspace of smooth ones. A character χ derives to an E-linear dχ: h ⊗_{Q_p} E → E, and χ is smooth iff dχ = 0; χ is locally σ-analytic when dχ factors through h ⊗_{K,σ} E, giving Hom_σ(H,E). For H = K^×: dim_E Hom_sm(K^×,E) = 1, dim_E Hom_σ(K^×,E) = 2, dim_E Hom(K^×,E) = 1 + d_K.

items.name: The Robba ring R_{K,E} and (φ,Γ)-modules over it
items.statement: R_{K,E} is the E-coefficient Robba ring for K: functions convergent on annuli of outer radius 1, with the Frobenius φ and the action of Γ = Gal(K_∞/K). A (φ,Γ)-module over R_{K,E} is a finite free R_{K,E}-module with commuting semilinear φ and Γ actions such that φ^*M ≅ M.
items.locator: §2.1, p. 10 (‘Let R_{K,E} be the E-coefficient Robba ring for K’)
items.note: PG.7 is written for the affinoid/relative Robba category of Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao; P7:annulus-foundations builds the Robba coefficient rings themselves.

items.name: Rank-one (φ,Γ)-modules R_{K,E}(χ) and their de Rham locus
items.statement: To a continuous character χ: K^× → E^× is attached the rank one (φ,Γ)-module R_{K,E}(χ) over R_{K,E} (Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao §6.2); every rank one module arises this way, and R_{K,E}(χ) is de Rham if and only if χ is locally algebraic.
items.note: Cited as [44, §6.2] (Kedlaya–Pottharst–Xiao). The unit for the paper: every trianguline parameter is a character of T(K) read through this dictionary.

items.name: Ext^i of (φ,Γ)-modules and (φ,Γ)-cohomology
items.statement: Ext^i(M,N) (written without ‘(φ,Γ)’ in the subscript) is the i-th extension group in the category of (φ,Γ)-modules over R_{K,E}, computed by the Herr complex of Hom_{R_{K,E}}(M,N); H^i_{(φ,Γ)}(M) denotes the cohomology of M. Liu's Euler characteristic formula and the vanishing of H^2 in the generic case are used throughout to compute dimensions.
items.note: PG.3 owns the Herr complex and its finiteness; the Euler characteristic formula of Liu is exactly what PG.3 must export.

items.name: Elements of Ext^1(M,M) as deformations over R_{K,E[ε]/ε²}
items.statement: An element of Ext^1(M,M) is identified with a deformation of M over R_{K,E[ε]/ε²}: the E[ε]/ε²-structure on an extension M̃ is given by letting ε act through M̃ ↠ M --id--> M ↪ M̃. All the deformation spaces of the paper are subspaces of Ext^1(M,M) under this identification.

items.name: De Rham extensions Ext^1_g(M,N)
items.statement: For de Rham (φ,Γ)-modules M and N, Ext^1_g(M,N) ⊂ Ext^1(M,N) is the subspace of extensions that are again de Rham.

items.name: The functors W^+_dR, its σ-decomposition, and D^+_dR
items.statement: W^+_dR(M) is the semilinear Gal_K-representation over B^+_dR ⊗_{Q_p} E attached to M (Berger, Prop. 2.2.6 (2)), with the decomposition W^+_dR(M) ≅ ⊕_{σ∈Σ_K} W^+_{dR,σ}(M) coming from B^+_dR ⊗_{Q_p} E ≅ ⊕_σ B^+_dR ⊗_{K,σ} E; D^+_dR(M) := W^+_dR(M)^{Gal_K} ≅ ⊕_σ D^+_dR(M)_σ.
items.note: The σ-decomposition of B^+_dR ⊗_{Q_p} E is what makes every ‘partially de Rham’ statement of the paper possible.

items.name: B-pairs and the comparison of (φ,Γ)-cohomology with Galois cohomology
items.statement: W(M) = (W_e(M), W^+_dR(M)) is the B-pair attached to M (Berger), and for i = 0,1,2 there are natural isomorphisms H^i_{(φ,Γ)}(M) ≅ H^i(Gal_K, W(M)) with the Galois cohomology of the B-pair (Nakamura, Thm. 5.11).
items.note: Used to import Ding's partially de Rham dimension formulas (his [31, Cor. A.4, Prop. A.5]) into (φ,Γ)-module deformation theory.

items.name: Lemma 2.1: torsion quotients are computed by D^+_dR
items.statement: Let N ⊂ M be (φ,Γ)-modules over R_{K,E} of the same rank. Then there is a natural isomorphism of E-vector spaces H^0_{(φ,Γ)}(M/N) ≅ H^0(Gal_K, W^+_dR(M)/W^+_dR(N)); when M is de Rham this identifies H^0_{(φ,Γ)}(M/N) with D^+_dR(M)/D^+_dR(N).
items.note: The workhorse of every dimension count in §§2.2–2.4: it converts a kernel of a push-forward map into a difference of D^+_dR-dimensions, which is read off from Hodge–Tate–Sen weights.

items.name: Crystabelline (φ,Γ)-modules and their filtered Deligne–Fontaine modules
items.statement: A (φ,Γ)-module M of rank d over R_{K,E} is crystabelline when it becomes crystalline over an abelian extension K'/K. To it are attached D_pst(M) = (W_e(M) ⊗_{B_e} B_cris)^{Gal_{K'}}, free of rank d over K'_0 ⊗_{Q_p} E with commuting semilinear φ and Gal(K'/K)-actions, and D_dR(M) := (W^+_dR(M)[1/t])^{Gal_K} ≅ (D_pst(M) ⊗_{K'_0} K')^{Gal(K'/K)}, free of rank d over K ⊗_{Q_p} E and carrying the Hodge filtration Fil_H by K ⊗_{Q_p} E-submodules (not necessarily free).
items.note: The pair (D_pst, D_dR with Fil_H) is the object whose ‘Hodge parameter’ the whole paper is about.

items.name: The Weil–Deligne representation r(M) and genericity
items.statement: To D_pst(M) is attached a Weil–Deligne representation r(M) over E (Berger–Schneider, Prop. 4.1). M is generic when r(M) is semisimple and isomorphic to ⊕_{i=1}^d φ_i with φ_iφ_j^{-1} ≠ 1, |·|_K for i ≠ j. Equivalently, M is generic crystabelline iff there are smooth characters φ_1,…,φ_d of K^× with M[1/t] ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^d R_{K,E}(φ_i)[1/t] and φ_iφ_j^{-1} ≠ 1, |·|_K for i ≠ j.
items.note: The two genericity conditions φ_iφ_j^{-1} ≠ 1 and ≠ |·|_K are what force Hom(D,D) = E and Ext^2(D,D) = 0; every dimension formula of §2.3 rests on them.

items.name: Refinements of a generic crystabelline module and the filtrations T_w
items.statement: An ordering of (φ_1,…,φ_d) is a refinement of M. For w ∈ S_d the ordering w(φ) = (φ_{w^{-1}(1)},…,φ_{w^{-1}(d)}) corresponds to a unique increasing filtration T_w = {T_w^i} of saturated (φ,Γ)-submodules of M with (gr^i_{T_w} M)[1/t] ≅ R_{K,E}(φ_{w^{-1}(i)})[1/t]. The tuple w(φ) is viewed as a smooth character of the diagonal torus T(K) ⊂ GL_d(K) and is also called a refinement.
items.note: The dictionary ‘refinement = element of S_d = character of T(K)’ is what lets the Galois side and the GL_n(K) side be compared refinement by refinement.

items.name: Non-critical refinements, ΦΓ_nc(φ,h), and regular Hodge–Tate–Sen weights
items.statement: Let h = (h_{σ,1} ≥ … ≥ h_{σ,d})_{σ∈Σ_K} be the Hodge–Tate–Sen weights of M, normalised so that the cyclotomic character has weight 1. The refinement w(φ) (equivalently T_w) is non-critical when the weights of gr^i_{T_w} M are exactly h_i; M is non-critical when all of its refinements are. ΦΓ_nc(φ,h) is the set of isomorphism classes of non-critical crystabelline (φ,Γ)-modules with refinement φ and weights h. The weights are regular when h_{σ,i} > h_{σ,i+1} for all σ.
items.note: Non-criticality of ALL refinements (not just one) is the standing hypothesis; it is what makes the amalgamation map (2.17) surjective and the induction of Theorem 3.21 work.

items.name: The subquotients M_r and M^r attached to a subset of a refinement
items.statement: For a generic crystabelline M with refinement φ and r = {r_1,…,r_k} ⊂ {1,…,d}, M_r (resp. M^r) is the saturated (φ,Γ)-submodule of M (resp. quotient of M) with refinement (φ_{r_1},…,φ_{r_k}); M^r = M/M_{r^c}. If M is non-critical then so are M_r and M^r, with Hodge–Tate–Sen weights (h_1,…,h_k) and (h_{d-k+1},…,h_d).
items.note: These depend on the chosen refinement; the paper fixes the refinement by context. Used constantly to cut D into D_1 = D_{{1,…,n-1}} and C_1 = D^{{1,…,n-1}}.

items.name: The submodule D_1, the quotient C_1 and the map ι_D
items.statement: For D ∈ ΦΓ_nc(φ,h) with strictly decreasing weights, set D_1 := D_{{1,…,n-1}} and C_1 := D^{{1,…,n-1}}, giving exact sequences 0 → D_1 → D → R_{K,E}(φ_n z^{h_n}) → 0 and 0 → R_{K,E}(φ_n z^{h_1}) → D → C_1 → 0. The composition ι_D: D_1 ↪ D ↠ C_1 is injective because Hom(D_1, R_{K,E}(φ_n z^{h_1})) = 0.
items.note: ι_D is the paper's reinterpretation of the p-adic Hodge parameter: an element of the (at most 2-dimensional) space Hom(D_1,C_1), taken up to scalar.

items.name: Vanishing of Hom between rank one modules
items.note: Elementary but used in every dévissage of §§2.2–2.4.

items.name: Proposition 2.2: Hom(D_1,C_1) is at most two-dimensional, and when it is two-dimensional
items.statement: (1) dim_E Hom(D_1,C_1) ≤ 2. (2) dim_E Hom(D_1,C_1) = 2 if and only if n ≥ 3 and for every i ∈ {1,…,n-1}, with r := {1,…,n-1}∖{i}, one has (D_1)^r ≅ (C_1)_r for the refinement (φ_1,…,φ_{n-1}); in that case the compositions α_i: D_1 ↠ (D_1)^r ≅ (C_1)_r ↪ C_1 are pairwise linearly independent in Hom(D_1,C_1).
items.note: Remark 2.3 adds that Hom(D_1,C_1) is always two-dimensional for n = 3, and for n = 4 with K = Q_p; in general its dimension is 1 or 2 depending on D_1 and C_1.

items.name: The cup product pairing that detects D
items.statement: The cup product Ext^1(R_{K,E}(φ_n z^{h_n}), D_1) × Hom(D_1,C_1) → Ext^1(R_{K,E}(φ_n z^{h_n}), C_1); pairing with a fixed ι ∈ Hom(D_1,C_1) is the push-forward map along ι.

items.name: Proposition 2.4: ι_D determines D when K = Q_p
items.statement: Under the cup product (2.6), E[D] ⊂ [ι_D]^⊥, with equality when K = Q_p. Consequently, for K = Q_p, D is determined by D_1, C_1, φ_n and ι_D: if D' is a crystabelline module of rank n over R_{Q_p,E} with saturated submodule D_1, quotient C_1 and refinement (φ_1,…,φ_n) such that ι_{D'} equals ι_D up to a non-zero scalar, then D' ≅ D.
items.note: The proof computes the kernel of the composite push-forward as D^+_dR(C'_1)/D^+_dR(D'_1), of dimension d_K, by Lemma 2.1; this is exactly why the statement degenerates for K ≠ Q_p and has to be replaced by the σ-by-σ statement of Proposition 2.8.

items.name: The weight 𝔗_σ(h) and the operation D ↦ D_σ on weights
items.statement: For σ ∈ Σ_K, 𝔗_σ(h) is the weight with 𝔗_σ(h)_{τ,i} = h_{τ,i} for τ = σ and h_{τ,n} for τ ≠ σ; it is constant in i away from σ.

items.name: Proposition 2.5: the partial modification D_σ and its filtered φ-module
items.statement: (1) For D ∈ ΦΓ_nc(φ,h) and σ ∈ Σ_K there is a unique (φ,Γ)-module D_σ over R_{K,E} with D_σ[1/t] ≅ D[1/t], D ⊂ D_σ and Hodge–Tate weights 𝔗_σ(h). (2) The injection D ↪ D_σ induces an isomorphism of Deligne–Fontaine modules D_pst(D) ≅ D_pst(D_σ) under which D_dR(D) → D_dR(D_σ) is a morphism of filtered K ⊗_{Q_p} E-modules restricting to an isomorphism D_dR(D)_σ ≅ D_dR(D_σ) of filtered E-vector spaces.
items.note: Constructed from Fontaine's classification of B_dR-representations applied to the B-pair of D: Λ_τ = W^+_dR(D)_τ for τ = σ and (t^{h_{τ,n}}B^+_dR ⊗_{K,τ} E)^{⊕n} otherwise. D_σ keeps only the σ-component of the Hodge filtration.

items.name: Fontaine's classification of B_dR-representations
items.statement: The classification of B^+_dR ⊗_{Q_p} E-representations of Gal_K used to produce the lattice Λ with W^+_dR(D) ⊂ Λ ⊂ W^+_dR(D)[1/t] prescribed componentwise (Fontaine, ‘Arithmétique des représentations galoisiennes p-adiques’, Thm. 3.19), together with Berger's theorem that a B-pair determines a (φ,Γ)-module.
items.locator: used in the proof of Proposition 2.5, p. 13
items.note: This is the same input that Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen use for almost de Rham representations; PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 routes it to P7 as well.

items.name: Lemma 2.6: every refinement survives the modification
items.statement: For D and D_σ as in Proposition 2.5 and every w ∈ S_n, the character w(φ) z^{𝔗_σ(h)} is a trianguline parameter of D_σ.
items.note: Hence D_σ ∈ ΦΓ_nc(φ, 𝔗_σ(h)): the modification preserves non-criticality of all refinements.

items.name: The surjection 𝔗_σ: ΦΓ_nc(φ,h) → ΦΓ_nc(φ,𝔗_σ(h))
items.statement: D ↦ D_σ defines a surjective map 𝔗_σ: ΦΓ_nc(φ,h) → ΦΓ_nc(φ,𝔗_σ(h)); it is applied to D and to its subquotients, giving D_{1,σ} = 𝔗_σ(D_1) and C_{1,σ} = 𝔗_σ(C_1), which are the rank n-1 subobject and quotient of D_σ for the refinement φ.
items.note: The family {D_σ}_{σ∈Σ_K} is the set of Hodge parameters that the GL_n(K)-side will see; for K ≠ Q_p it is strictly weaker than D itself.

items.name: Proposition 2.7: the σ-analogue of Proposition 2.2
items.statement: (1) dim_E Hom(D_{1,σ},C_{1,σ}) ≤ 2. (2) It equals 2 if and only if n ≥ 3 and (D_{1,σ})^r ≅ (C_{1,σ})_r for every i (with r = {1,…,n-1}∖{i}), in which case the maps α_{i,σ}: D_{1,σ} ↠ (D_{1,σ})^r ≅ (C_{1,σ})_r ↪ C_{1,σ} are pairwise linearly independent.

items.name: Proposition 2.8: ι_{D_σ} determines D_σ
items.statement: For the cup product Ext^1(R_{K,E}(φ_n z^{h_n}), D_{1,σ}) × Hom(D_{1,σ},C_{1,σ}) → Ext^1(R_{K,E}(φ_n z^{h_n}), C_{1,σ}) one has [ι_{D_σ}]^⊥ = E[D_σ]. In particular D_σ is determined by D_{1,σ}, C_{1,σ}, φ_n and ι_{D_σ} in the sense of Proposition 2.4.
items.note: The kernel of the relevant push-forward is one-dimensional here — by Lemma 2.1 it is a difference of D^+_dR's whose weights agree away from σ — which is exactly the gain over Proposition 2.4.

items.name: Example 2.9: the parameter a_{D_σ} for n = 3 and its reading from ι_{D_σ}
items.statement: For n = 3, K unramified and D crystalline generic non-critical with regular weights, D_cris(D_σ)_σ is a filtered φ^{d_K}-module with φ^{d_K}-eigenvectors e_{1,σ},e_{2,σ},e_{3,σ} normalised so that the maximal step of Fil D_cris(D_{1,σ})_σ is spanned by e_{1,σ}+e_{2,σ} and that of Fil D_cris(D_σ)_σ by e_{1,σ}+a_{D_σ}e_{2,σ}+e_{3,σ}; D_σ is determined by the single parameter a_{D_σ} ∈ E∖{0,1}, and a_{D_σ} is read off from the relative position of the line Fil^max D_cris(C_{1,σ})_σ and the line ι_{D_σ}(Fil^max D_cris(D_{1,σ})_σ) inside D_cris(C_{1,σ})_σ.
items.note: The concrete face of the whole paper: for GL_3 the new Hodge parameter is a single cross-ratio-like coordinate a_{D_σ}, invisible to (r, h) and to the classical local Langlands correspondence.

items.name: Deformations of a character and the isomorphism (2.10)
items.statement: For a continuous χ: K^× → E^× there are natural isomorphisms Hom(K^×,E) ≅ Ext^1_{K^×}(χ,χ) ≅ Ext^1(R_{K,E}(χ), R_{K,E}(χ)), sending ψ to χ(1+ψε) and then to R_{K,E[ε]/ε²}(χ(1+ψε)).

items.name: Trianguline deformations Ext^1_w(D,D), the trianguline parameter and the weight map κ_w
items.statement: For w ∈ S_n, Ext^1_w(D,D) ⊂ Ext^1(D,D) is the subspace of D̃ that are successive extensions of R_{K,E[ε]/ε²}(φ_{w^{-1}(i)} z^{h_i}(1+ψ_iε)) for ψ_i ∈ Hom(K^×,E); the character w(φ)z^h(1+ψε) of T(K) over E[ε]/ε² is the trianguline parameter of D̃ with respect to w(φ). κ_w: Ext^1_w(D,D) → Ext^1_{T(K)}(w(φ)z^h, w(φ)z^h) ≅ Hom(T(K),E) sends D̃ to its parameter. The notation Ext^1_{T_w}(D,D) is also used.
items.note: κ_w is the ‘weight map’ whose fibres the whole comparison with GL_n(K) is built on; Hom(T(K),E) has dimension n(1+d_K).

items.name: Proposition 2.10: dimensions of the deformation spaces
items.statement: (1) dim_E Ext^1(D,D) = 1 + n²d_K, dim_E Ext^1_g(D,D) = 1 + (n(n-1)/2)d_K, and dim_E Ext^1_w(D,D) = 1 + (n(n+1)/2)d_K for every w ∈ S_n. (2) κ_w is surjective for every w. (3) Ext^1_g(D,D) ⊂ Ext^1_w(D,D) and equals the preimage of Hom_sm(T(K),E) under κ_w.
items.note: Proved from Hom(D,D) = E, Ext^2(D,D) = 0 (genericity), Liu's Euler characteristic, and Nakamura's Cor. 2.53 / Prop. 2.41 / Lem. 2.56; the case K = Q_p is Bellaïche–Chenevier Prop. 2.3.10, Thm. 2.5.10.

items.name: The S_n-action on Hom(T(K),E)
items.statement: S_n acts on T(K) on the right by w(a_1,…,a_n) = (a_{w(1)},…,a_{w(n)}), inducing the left action (wψ)(a_1,…,a_n) = ψ(a_{w(1)},…,a_{w(n)}) on Hom(T(K),E); Hom_sm(T(K),E) is stable.

items.name: Lemma 2.11: the weight maps for different refinements differ by the Weyl action
items.statement: For w_1,w_2 ∈ S_n the square with vertical identity on Ext^1_g(D,D), horizontal maps κ_{w_1}, κ_{w_2} and right vertical map w_2w_1^{-1} on Hom_sm(T(K),E) commutes.
items.note: Proved by comparing the two triangulations step by step; this is what makes Ext^1_0(D,D) = Ker κ_w independent of w.

items.name: Ext^1_0(D,D), the quotients \bar{Ext}^1_*(D,D) and their dimensions
items.statement: Ext^1_0(D,D) := Ker κ_w is independent of w, is contained in Ext^1_g(D,D), and has dimension (n(n-1)/2)d_K + 1 - n. For Ext^1_*(D,D) ⊃ Ext^1_0(D,D) one sets \bar{Ext}^1_*(D,D) := Ext^1_*(D,D)/Ext^1_0(D,D); then κ_w gives isomorphisms \bar{Ext}^1_w(D,D) ≅ Hom(T(K),E) and \bar{Ext}^1_g(D,D) ≅ Hom_sm(T(K),E), and dim_E \bar{Ext}^1(D,D) = (n(n+1)/2)d_K + n.
items.note: \bar{Ext}^1(D,D), of dimension (n(n+1)/2)d_K + n, is the target of the map t_D of Theorem 3.21 — the Galois-side object that the GL_n(K)-representation must reproduce.

items.name: De Rham deformations up to twist: Ext^1_{g'}(D,D) and Hom_{g'}(T(K),E)
items.statement: Hom_{g'}(T(K),E) is the space of ψ ∈ Hom(T(K),E) such that ψ - ψ_0∘det is smooth for some ψ_0: K^× → E; Ext^1_{g'}(D,D) ⊂ Ext^1(D,D) is the subspace of deformations that are de Rham up to a twist by a character of K^× over (E[ε]/ε²)^×. It equals κ_w^{-1}(Hom_{g'}(T(K),E)) for every w, so dim_E Ext^1_{g'}(D,D) = 1 + ((n(n-1)/2)+1)d_K, and Lemma 2.11 holds with g replaced by g'.
items.note: Ext^1_{g'} is the precise Galois counterpart of the extensions of π_alg by itself: dim Hom_{g'}(T(K),E) = n + d_K = dim Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg, π_alg).

items.name: Proposition 2.12: trianguline deformations generate all deformations
items.statement: The natural map ⊕_{w∈S_n} Ext^1_w(D,D) → Ext^1(D,D) is surjective, and induces a surjection ⊕_{w∈S_n} \bar{Ext}^1_w(D,D) ↠ \bar{Ext}^1(D,D).
items.note: Chenevier Thm. 3.19 (K = Q_p) and Nakamura Thm. 2.62 in general; it uses that ALL refinements of D are non-critical. The paper also reproves it from its own Corollary 2.33 by induction.

items.name: P-filtrations and F_P-deformations
items.statement: For a standard parabolic P ⊃ B of GL_n with Levi L_P = diag(GL_{n_1},…,GL_{n_r}), a filtration F_P: 0 = Fil^0 ⊊ Fil^1 ⊊ … ⊊ Fil^r = D by saturated (φ,Γ)-submodules is a P-filtration when rank gr^i_{F_P} D = n_i, and one writes M_i := gr^i_{F_P} D. A deformation D̃ of D over E[ε]/ε² is an F_P-deformation when it carries a filtration of saturated (φ,Γ)-submodules over R_{K,E[ε]/ε²} whose graded pieces deform the M_i; these form Ext^1_{F_P}(D,D) ⊂ Ext^1(D,D).
items.note: Source issue: the printed sentence defines ‘M_i := rank gr^i_{F_P} D = n_i’, making M_i an integer, although M_i is used as a (φ,Γ)-module immediately after; and it writes E[ε/ε²] and ‘submodules of D’ for ‘of D̃’.

items.name: Proposition 2.13: dimension and surjectivity for paraboline deformations
items.statement: dim_E Ext^1_{F_P}(D,D) = 1 + d_K dim P = 1 + d_K Σ_{1≤i≤j≤r} n_i n_j, and the natural map κ_{F_P}: Ext^1_{F_P}(D,D) → ∏_{i=1}^r Ext^1(M_i,M_i), D̃ ↦ (gr^i_{F_P} D̃), is surjective.
items.note: Chenevier Prop. 3.6, 3.7 for K = Q_p; the paper notes the arguments generalise verbatim, and gives the general proof in Proposition 2.17.

items.name: Corollary 2.14: paraboline deformations are the product of their graded deformations
items.statement: Let T_w be compatible with F_P (T_w induces a complete flag on each Fil^i_{F_P} D). (1) Ext^1_w(D,D) is the preimage of ∏_i Ext^1_{T_{w,i}}(M_i,M_i) under κ_{F_P}, and κ_{F_P}: Ext^1_w(D,D) ↠ ∏_i Ext^1_{T_{w,i}}(M_i,M_i). (2) κ_{F_P} sends Ext^1_0(D,D) into ∏_i Ext^1_0(M_i,M_i) and induces isomorphisms \bar{Ext}^1_{F_P}(D,D) ≅ ∏_i \bar{Ext}^1(M_i,M_i) and \bar{Ext}^1_w(D,D) ≅ ∏_i \bar{Ext}^1_{T_{w,i}}(M_i,M_i).
items.note: Source issue: the printed dimension check in the proof reads d_K dim(B ∩ L_P) − n where it must be + n. The isomorphism (2.19) is the Galois half of the compatibility with parabolic induction (Proposition 3.27).

items.name: Corollary 2.15: the Weyl-equivariance for paraboline g'-deformations
items.statement: With Hom_{P,g'}(T(K),E) := {ψ : ψ - ψ_P∘det_{L_P} smooth for some ψ_P: Z_{L_P}(K) → E} (of dimension n + rd_K) and Ext^1_{F_P,g'}(D,D) the preimage of ∏_i Ext^1_{g'}(M_i,M_i): (1) if T_w is compatible with F_P then Ext^1_{F_P,g'}(D,D) ⊂ Ext^1_w(D,D); (2) for T_{w_1}, T_{w_2} compatible with F_P (so w_2w_1^{-1} ∈ W_P), κ_{w_1} and κ_{w_2} differ by the action of w_2w_1^{-1} on Hom_{P,g'}(T(K),E).
items.note: This is the source of the ‘higher intertwining’ of §2.4 and of the key step of Theorem 3.21 for the refinements w with 1 < w(n) < n.

items.name: J-de Rham (φ,Γ)-modules and the σ-partial deformation spaces
items.statement: For J ⊂ Σ_K, M is J-de Rham when dim_E D_dR(M)_τ = rank M for all τ ∈ J, where D_dR(M)_τ = H^0(Gal_K, W^+_dR(M)_τ[1/t]); the property passes to subquotients. For an extension group Ext^1_?(D,D), Ext^1_{σ,?}(D,D) is the subspace of D̃ that are Σ_K∖{σ}-de Rham, and \bar{Ext}^1_{σ,?}(D,D) its image modulo Ext^1_0(D,D).
items.note: This is the device that reduces the case of a general K to one embedding at a time: the σ-part of the Hodge filtration is the only information that survives.

items.name: Lemma 2.16: dimension of the partially de Rham deformation space
items.note: Proved by identifying Ext^1_σ(D,D) with H^1_{g,Σ_K∖{σ}}(Gal_K, W(D ⊗ D^∨)) and applying Ding's partially de Rham dimension formula [31, Cor. A.4]. Source issue: the weights are printed with indices i,j = 1,…,r instead of 1,…,n.

items.name: Proposition 2.17: partially de Rham paraboline deformations
items.statement: (1) dim_E Ext^1_{σ,F_P}(D,D) = 1 + (d_K - 1)(n(n-1)/2) + dim P. (2) The map κ_{F_P}: Ext^1_{σ,F_P}(D,D) → ∏_i Ext^1_σ(M_i,M_i) is surjective and induces an isomorphism \bar{Ext}_{σ,F_P}(D,D) ≅ ∏_i \bar{Ext}^1_σ(M_i,M_i).
items.note: The proof introduces Hom_{F_P}(D,D) ⊂ D ⊗ D^∨, the submodule of endomorphisms preserving the filtration, whose Hodge–Tate–Sen weights are indexed by the entries of gl_n lying in p.

items.name: Corollary 2.18: compatibility of the σ-theory with compatible refinements
items.statement: If T_w is a B-filtration compatible with F_P then κ_{F_P} induces a bijection \bar{Ext}^1_{σ,w}(D,D) ≅ ∏_i \bar{Ext}^1_{σ,T_{w,i}}(M_i,M_i).

items.name: Locally σ-analytic deformations of a rank one module, and Corollary 2.19
items.statement: For a rank one de Rham R_{K,E}(χ), (2.10) restricts to an isomorphism Ext^1_σ(R_{K,E}(χ),R_{K,E}(χ)) ≅ Hom_σ(K^×,E) (Ding, [31, Lem. 1.15]); hence for every w ∈ S_n, κ_w induces an isomorphism \bar{Ext}_{σ,w}(D,D) ≅ Hom_σ(T(K),E).
items.note: Hom_σ(T(K),E) has dimension 2n; this is the σ-analogue of \bar{Ext}^1_w(D,D) ≅ Hom(T(K),E).

items.name: Proposition 2.20: deformations of the modified module D_σ
items.statement: (1) dim_E Ext^1(D_σ,D_σ) = 1 + n²d_K. (2) dim_E Ext^1_g(D_σ,D_σ) = 1 + n(n-1)/2. (3) For a P-filtration F_P of D_σ with graded pieces M_{i,σ}: dim_E Ext^1_{F_P}(D_σ,D_σ) = 1 + d_K dim P, Ext^1_g(D_σ,D_σ) ⊂ Ext^1_{F_P}(D_σ,D_σ), and Ext^1_{F_P}(D_σ,D_σ) ↠ ∏_i Ext^1(M_{i,σ},M_{i,σ}).
items.note: Remark 2.21 observes that for K ≠ Q_p, Ext^1_g(D_σ,D_σ) is strictly smaller than κ_w^{-1}(Hom_sm(T(K),E)) — the first place where D_σ behaves differently from D.

items.name: Proposition 2.22: partially de Rham deformations of D_σ
items.statement: (1) dim_E Ext^1_σ(D_σ,D_σ) = 1 + n². (2) For a standard parabolic P and a P-filtration F_P of D_σ, dim_E Ext^1_{σ,F_P}(D_σ,D_σ) = 1 + dim P.

items.name: Proposition 2.23: the modification of a deformation
items.statement: For every D̃ ∈ Ext^1(D,D) over R_{K,E[ε]/ε²} there is a unique D̃_σ ∈ Ext^1(D_σ,D_σ) with D̃ ⊂ D̃_σ, D̃[1/t] ≅ D̃_σ[1/t], the same Sen σ-weights as D̃, and Sen τ-weights constantly h_{τ,n} for τ ≠ σ; this defines 𝔗_σ: Ext^1(D,D) → Ext^1(D_σ,D_σ), which preserves partial de Rhamness and filtrations by saturated submodules.

items.name: Proposition 2.24: 𝔗_σ is surjective with kernel of dimension (d_K-1)n(n-1)/2
items.statement: (1) For * ∈ {g, σ, {σ,F_P}} the induced map 𝔗_σ: Ext^1_*(D,D) → Ext^1_*(D_σ,D_σ) is surjective with the same kernel as (2.27), of dimension (d_K - 1)n(n-1)/2. (2) The square relating κ_{F_P} on D and on D_σ commutes and Ext^1_{σ,F_P}(D_σ,D_σ) ↠ ∏_i Ext^1_σ(M_{i,σ},M_{i,σ}).
items.note: Computed from Lemma 2.1: dim D^+_dR(D_σ ⊗ D^∨) = n(n+1)/2 + (d_K-1)n² and dim D^+_dR(D ⊗ D^∨) = (n(n+1)/2)d_K.

items.name: Corollaries 2.25–2.27: Ext^1_0(D_σ,D_σ) and the induced isomorphisms on \bar{Ext}
items.statement: Corollary 2.25: the weight maps κ_w on Ext^1_g(D_σ,D_σ) are surjective and differ by the Weyl action. Ext^1_0(D_σ,D_σ) is defined as their common kernel. Corollary 2.26: Ext^1_0(D,D) = 𝔗_σ^{-1}(Ext^1_0(D_σ,D_σ)) and 𝔗_σ restricts to a surjection on Ext^1_0. Corollary 2.27: for * ∈ {σ, g, {F_P,σ}}, 𝔗_σ induces isomorphisms \bar{Ext}^1_*(D,D) ≅ \bar{Ext}^1_*(D_σ,D_σ) compatible with κ_{F_P}.
items.note: These are the identifications that let the GL_n(K)-side, which only ever sees \bar{Ext}^1_σ, detect D_σ rather than D.

items.name: The two filtrations F and G on D and their deformation spaces
items.statement: F is the filtration D_1 ⊂ D and G is R_{K,E}(φ_n z^{h_1}) ⊂ D, corresponding to (2.1) and (2.2). By Proposition 2.13, dim_E Ext^1_F(D,D) = dim_E Ext^1_G(D,D) = 1 + (n²-n+1)d_K, with surjections κ_F = (κ_{F,1},κ_{F,2}): Ext^1_F(D,D) ↠ Ext^1(D_1,D_1) × Hom(K^×,E) and κ_G = (κ_{G,1},κ_{G,2}): Ext^1_G(D,D) ↠ Ext^1(C_1,C_1) × Hom(K^×,E).
items.note: ‘Higher intertwining’ in this paper means: a single deformation D̃ carries BOTH an F- and a G-filtration by saturated submodules over R_{K,E[ε]/ε²}.

items.name: The subspaces Ext^1_ι(D_1,D_1) and Ext^1_ι(C_1,C_1) attached to ι ∈ Hom(D_1,C_1)
items.statement: For ι ∈ Hom(D_1,C_1) let ι^-: Ext^1(C_1,D_1) → Ext^1(D_1,D_1) be the pull-back and ι^+: Ext^1(C_1,D_1) → Ext^1(C_1,C_1) the push-forward; set Ext^1_ι(D_1,D_1) := Im(ι^-) and Ext^1_ι(C_1,C_1) := Im(ι^+).
items.note: These subspaces are the Galois-side avatar of the Hodge parameter: by Proposition 2.29 (3) they determine ι up to a scalar.

items.name: Lemma 2.28: dimensions for the degenerate maps α_i
items.statement: Assume dim_E Hom(D_1,C_1) = 2 and let α_i be as in Proposition 2.2. Then dim_E Ext^1_{α_i}(D_1,D_1) = (n-1)(n-2)d_K; for j ≠ i, dim_E(Ext^1_{α_i} ∩ Ext^1_{α_j})(D_1,D_1) = (n-1)(n-3)d_K + d_K - 1, hence dim_E(Ext^1_{α_i} + Ext^1_{α_j})(D_1,D_1) = 1 + n(n-2)d_K. The same holds with D_1 replaced by C_1.
items.note: The point of the computation: the sum for i ≠ j is strictly bigger than dim Ext^1_ι(D_1,D_1) = 1 + (n-1)(n-2)d_K, which is what forces ι to be determined up to scalar in Proposition 2.29 (3).

items.name: Proposition 2.29: Ext^1_ι determines ι up to a scalar
items.statement: Let ι ∈ Hom(D_1,C_1) be injective. (1) dim_E Ext^1_ι(D_1,D_1) = dim_E Ext^1_ι(C_1,C_1) = 1 + (n-1)(n-2)d_K. (2) Ext^1_g(D_1,D_1) ⊂ Ext^1_ι(D_1,D_1) and Ext^1_g(C_1,C_1) ⊂ Ext^1_ι(C_1,C_1). (3) For ι' ∈ Hom(D_1,C_1): Ext^1_{ι'}(D_1,D_1) = Ext^1_ι(D_1,D_1) ⟺ Ext^1_{ι'}(C_1,C_1) = Ext^1_ι(C_1,C_1) ⟺ ι' = aι for some a ∈ E^×.

items.name: Lemma 2.30: ι^- and ι^+ have the same weight
items.statement: For M ∈ Ext^1_g(C_1,D_1), κ_{φ^1}∘ι_g^-(M) = κ_{φ^1}∘ι_g^+(M), where ι_g^± are the restrictions of ι^± to Ext^1_g(C_1,D_1) and κ_{φ^1} is the weight map for the refinement φ^1 = φ_1 ⊠ … ⊠ φ_{n-1}.
items.note: Proved by the commutative ladder relating ι_g^-(M) and ι_g^+(M) through ι; it is what makes the set I_ι below well behaved.

items.name: ΦΓ_nc(D_1,C_1,φ_n) and the set I_ι of matched pairs
items.statement: ΦΓ_nc(D_1,C_1,φ_n) ⊂ ΦΓ_nc(φ,h) is the subset of D with Hom(D_1,D) = Hom(D,C_1) ≅ E, for fixed crystabelline D_1 (weights h^1) and C_1 (weights h^2) with a common generic refinement φ^1. For an injection ι ∈ Hom(D_1,C_1), I_ι is the set of pairs (D̃_1,C̃_1) ∈ Ext^1_ι(D_1,D_1) × Ext^1_ι(C_1,C_1) for which there is M ∈ Ext^1(C_1,D_1) with ι^-(M) = D̃_1 and -ι^+(M) = C̃_1; I_D := I_{ι_D}.
items.note: Corollary 2.31: I_ι = I_{ι'} iff ι' = aι, and for D,D' ∈ ΦΓ_nc(D_1,C_1,φ_n), I_D = I_{D'} iff ι_D = aι_{D'}; when K = Q_p this is equivalent to D ≅ D'.

items.name: Theorem 2.32 (Higher intertwining)
items.statement: Let D ∈ ΦΓ_nc(D_1,C_1,φ_n) and D̃ ∈ Ext^1_F(D,D) with κ_F(D̃) = (D̃_1,ψ). The following are equivalent: (1) D̃ ∈ Ext^1_F(D,D) ∩ Ext^1_G(D,D); (2) D̃_1 ⊗ R_{K,E[ε]/ε²}(1-ψε) ∈ Ext^1_{ι_D}(D_1,D_1). If they hold then κ_{G,2}(D̃) = ψ and there is M ∈ Ext^1(C_1,D_1) with D̃_1 = ι_D^-(M) ⊗ R_{K,E[ε]/ε²}(1+ψε) and κ_{G,1}(D̃) = ι_D^+(M) ⊗ R_{K,E[ε]/ε²}(1+ψε).
items.note: The central Galois-side theorem of §2: the deformations admitting two different parabolic filtrations are exactly those whose graded deformation lies in the subspace cut out by the Hodge parameter ι_D. Source issue: the second tensor factor is printed R_{E[ε]/ε²} without the K.

items.name: Corollary 2.33: F- and G-deformations already generate everything
items.statement: dim_E(Ext^1_F(D,D) ∩ Ext^1_G(D,D)) = 1 + (n²-2n+2)d_K, and consequently Ext^1_F(D,D) ⊕ Ext^1_G(D,D) ↠ Ext^1(D,D).
items.note: This gives an independent proof of Proposition 2.12 by induction. Source issue: the displayed dimension computation in the proof has unbalanced parentheses and subtracts the intersection without them.

items.name: The space V(D_1,C_1) and the subspace L(D,D_1,C_1)
items.statement: V(D_1,C_1) := (\bar{Ext}^1(D_1,D_1) × Hom(K^×,E)) ⊕ (\bar{Ext}^1(C_1,C_1) × Hom(K^×,E)), identified with \bar{Ext}^1_F(D,D) ⊕ \bar{Ext}^1_G(D,D) by (κ_F,κ_G); L(D,D_1,C_1) ⊂ V(D_1,C_1) consists of the ((D̃_1,ψ),(C̃_1,-ψ)) with (D̃_1 ⊗ R(1-ψε), C̃_1 ⊗ R(1+ψε)) ∈ I_D.
items.note: L(D,D_1,C_1) is the ‘higher intertwining subspace’: the kernel of the amalgamation, and the invariant that will be matched with a kernel on the GL_n(K)-side.

items.name: Corollary 2.34: L determines the Hodge parameter
items.statement: (1) For D,D' ∈ ΦΓ_nc(D_1,C_1,φ_n), L(D',D_1,C_1) = L(D,D_1,C_1) if and only if ι_{D'} = aι_D for some a ∈ E^×; when K = Q_p this is equivalent to D ≅ D'. (2) There is a natural exact sequence 0 → L(D,D_1,C_1) → V(D_1,C_1) → \bar{Ext}^1(D,D) → 0.
items.note: This is Theorem 1.7 of the introduction (‘D ≅ D' if and only if Ker(f_D) = Ker(f_{D'})’).

items.name: Proposition 2.35: the σ-analogue of Proposition 2.29
items.statement: For an injection ι_σ ∈ Hom(D_{1,σ},C_{1,σ}): (1) dim_E Ext^1_{ι_σ}(D_{1,σ},D_{1,σ}) = dim_E Ext^1_{ι_σ}(C_{1,σ},C_{1,σ}) = 1 + (n-1)(n-2); (2) Ext^1_g ⊂ Ext^1_{ι_σ} on both sides; (3) Ext^1_{ι'_σ} = Ext^1_{ι_σ} on either side if and only if ι'_σ = aι_σ for some a ∈ E^×.
items.note: Corollary 2.36: for D_σ,D'_σ ∈ ΦΓ_nc(D_{1,σ},C_{1,σ},φ_n), I_{D_σ} = I_{D'_σ} if and only if D_σ ≅ D'_σ — no longer only up to the ambiguity of Proposition 2.4.

items.name: Theorem 2.37: higher intertwining for partially de Rham deformations
items.statement: Let D̃_σ ∈ Ext^1_{σ,F}(D_σ,D_σ) with κ_F(D̃_σ) = (D̃_{1,σ},ψ). Then D̃_σ ∈ Ext^1_{σ,F}(D_σ,D_σ) ∩ Ext^1_{σ,G}(D_σ,D_σ) if and only if D̃_{1,σ} ⊗ R_{K,E[ε]/ε²}(1-ψε) ∈ Ext^1_{ι_{D_σ}}(D_{1,σ},D_{1,σ}); in that case κ_{G,2}(D̃_σ) = ψ and the graded pieces are given by an M ∈ Ext^1_σ(C_{1,σ},D_{1,σ}) as in Theorem 2.32.
items.note: Source issues: the parameter is printed D̃_{σ,1} in the hypothesis and D̃_{1,σ} in the conclusion, and the twisting module again loses its K.

items.name: Corollary 2.38: the σ-invariant L(D_σ,D_{1,σ},C_{1,σ})_σ determines D_σ
items.statement: With V(D_{1,σ},C_{1,σ})_σ := (\bar{Ext}^1_σ(D_{1,σ},D_{1,σ}) × Hom_σ(K^×,E)) ⊕ (\bar{Ext}^1_σ(C_{1,σ},C_{1,σ}) × Hom_σ(K^×,E)) and L(D_σ,D_{1,σ},C_{1,σ})_σ defined by the condition of Theorem 2.37: (1) L(D'_σ,…)_σ = L(D_σ,…)_σ if and only if D_σ ≅ D'_σ; (2) there is an exact sequence 0 → L(D_σ,D_{1,σ},C_{1,σ})_σ → V(D_{1,σ},C_{1,σ})_σ → \bar{Ext}^1_σ(D_σ,D_σ) → 0.
items.note: Source issue: the definition on p. 31 prints the third argument as D_{2,σ}, which is never defined (it must be C_{1,σ}), and Corollary 2.38 then drops the subscript σ from L(·)_σ.

items.name: Proposition 2.39: 𝔗_σ matches the two higher-intertwining sequences
items.statement: 𝔗_σ induces a commutative diagram of short exact sequences from 0 → L(D,D_1,C_1)_σ → V(D_1,C_1)_σ → \bar{Ext}^1_σ(D,D) → 0 to the sequence (2.42) for D_σ, in which all three vertical maps are isomorphisms; here V(D_1,C_1)_σ ⊂ V(D_1,C_1) is the locally σ-analytic part and L(D,D_1,C_1)_σ = L(D,D_1,C_1) ∩ V(D_1,C_1)_σ.

items.name: Corollary 2.40: partially de Rham trianguline deformations generate
items.statement: The map ⊕_{w∈S_n} Ext^1_{σ,w}(D,D) → Ext^1_σ(D,D) is surjective, and the same holds with D replaced by D_σ.
items.note: The σ-analogue of Proposition 2.12; proved from Proposition 2.39 by induction on n using Proposition 2.17 and Corollary 2.18.

items.name: Standard parabolics, the weights θ and θ^P, and the maximal parabolics P_i
items.statement: For a standard parabolic P ⊃ B of GL_n with Levi L_P ≅ GL_{n_1} × … × GL_{n_r}, θ := (0,-1,…,1-n) and θ^P := (0^{n_1}, (-n_1)^{n_2},…,(-(n_1+…+n_{r-1}))^{n_r}), viewed as an algebraic character of L_P (θ = θ^B). For i ∈ {1,…,n-1}, P_i is the maximal parabolic whose Levi L_i has simple roots {1,…,n-1}∖{i}, so L_{P_i} ≅ GL_i × GL_{n-i}.

items.name: Opposite Verma modules M^-(μ), their simple quotients L^-(μ), and L(λ)
items.statement: For a Lie algebra g over K set g_{Σ_K} := g ⊗_{Q_p} E ≅ ∏_σ g ⊗_{K,σ} E. For a weight μ of t_{Σ_K}, M^-(μ) := U(gl_{n,Σ_K}) ⊗_{U(b^-_{Σ_K})} μ with simple quotient L^-(μ); when μ is antidominant, L^-(μ) is finite dimensional and isomorphic to L(-μ)^∨, the dual of the algebraic representation of Res^K_{Q_p} GL_n of highest weight -μ.
items.note: A Tau Ceti roadmap already plans Verma modules and their simple quotients over a field of characteristic zero; here they are needed over E for the product Lie algebra gl_{n,Σ_K} = ∏_σ gl_n ⊗_{K,σ} E, i.e. for Res^K_{Q_p} GL_n. PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 imports the same layer.

items.name: Admissible locally Q_p-analytic representations, the distribution algebra and Ext groups
items.statement: For an admissible locally Q_p-analytic representation V of GL_n(K) over E, the continuous dual V^∨ is a coadmissible module over the Q_p-analytic distribution algebra D(GL_n(K),E) (Schneider–Teitelbaum). For admissible V_1,V_2 one sets Ext^i_{GL_n(K)}(V_1,V_2) := Ext^i_{D(GL_n(K),E)}(V_2^∨,V_1^∨) in the abelian category of abstract D(GL_n(K),E)-modules; by Breuil, Lem. 2.1.1, Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(V_1,V_2) is the group of extensions of V_1 by V_2 as admissible locally Q_p-analytic representations. Ext^1_lalg denotes the subgroup of locally algebraic extensions.
items.note: Nothing in the atlas builds the Schneider–Teitelbaum distribution algebra of a general p-adic group or its coadmissible modules; LocallyAnalyticDistributions L0 builds only Q_p-analytic distributions on O_F and finite products.

items.name: The E[ε]/ε²-structure on a self-extension and tautological/universal extensions
items.statement: Any Ṽ ∈ Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(V,V) carries a natural E[ε]/ε²-structure with ε acting through Ṽ ↠ V --id--> V ↪ Ṽ. For a subspace U ⊂ Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(V_1,V_2) (finite dimensional) there is a tautological extension of V_1 ⊗_E U by V_2; for U the whole Ext^1 it is called the universal extension of V_1 (or of V_1 ⊗_E Ext^1(V_1,V_2)) by V_2.
items.note: The universal extension is the object that carries the deformation-ring action in §3.2.2 and that is matched with a subspace of Π_∞ in §4.

items.name: Generic smooth characters of T(K), the modulus character and the smooth principal series I_sm(φ)
items.statement: φ = φ_1 ⊠ … ⊠ φ_n: T(K) → E^× smooth is generic when φ_iφ_j^{-1} ≠ 1, |·|_K for i ≠ j; δ_B is the modulus character of B(K) and η := 1 ⊠ |·|_K ⊠ … ⊠ |·|_K^{n-1} = |·|_K^{-1}∘θ. I_sm(φ) := (Ind_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)} φη)^∞ is absolutely irreducible admissible for generic φ, independent of the ordering: I_sm(φ) ≅ I_sm(w(φ)) =: π_sm(φ), and it is the representation attached to ⊕_i φ_i by the classical local Langlands correspondence.
items.note: SR.2 builds normalised parabolic induction and Jacquet functors, SR.3 admissibility, irreducibility criteria and the Bernstein decomposition; the irreducibility of a generic unramified-twist principal series and its independence of the ordering are exactly SR.3-type statements.

items.name: The dominant weight λ and the locally algebraic representation π_alg(φ,h)
items.statement: For h strictly dominant put λ := h - θ^{[K:Q_p]}, i.e. λ_{σ,i} = h_{σ,i} + i - 1, a dominant weight of t_{Σ_K}; π_alg(φ,h) := π_sm(φ) ⊗_E L(λ), an irreducible locally algebraic representation of GL_n(K), isomorphic to I_sm(w(φ)) ⊗_E L(λ) for every w.
items.note: π_alg(φ,h) is the locally algebraic representation predicted by classical local Langlands from (r,h); the entire paper is about what has to be glued to it to see the Hodge filtration.

items.name: The locally Q_p-analytic principal series PS(w(φ),h)
items.statement: PS(w(φ),h) := (Ind_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)} w(φ)ηz^λ)^{Q_p-an} = (Ind_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)} w(φ)z^h(ε^{-1}∘θ))^{Q_p-an}.

items.name: The Orlik–Strauch functor F^{GL_n}_{B^-}(-,-)
items.statement: The functor attaching to an object of category O for gl_{n,Σ_K} and a smooth representation of the Levi a locally Q_p-analytic representation of GL_n(K), together with the theorem of Orlik–Strauch describing its irreducible constituents and its exactness/adjunction properties.
items.note: Used for every structural statement about principal series in the paper. PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 also needs it (its ‘adjunction between Orlik–Strauch induction and Lie-algebra homomorphisms’).

items.name: Proposition 3.1: constituents and socle of the locally analytic principal series
items.statement: For w ∈ S_n: (1) the irreducible constituents of PS(w(φ),h) are the C(w,u) := F^{GL_n}_{B^-}(L^-(-u·λ), w(φ)η) for u = (u_σ) ∈ S_n^{|Σ_K|}, pairwise distinct, and those with lg(u) = 1 have multiplicity one; (2) soc PS(w(φ),h) ≅ I_sm(w(φ)) ⊗_E L(λ) ≅ π_alg(φ,h); (3) soc(PS(w(φ),h)/π_alg(φ,h)) ≅ ⊕_{lg(u)=1} C(w,u); (4) for lg(u) = lg(u') = 1, C(w,u) ≅ C(w',u') iff u = u' = s_{i,σ} for some i,σ and w(w')^{-1} lies in the Weyl group of L_{P_i}.
items.note: (1),(4) from Orlik–Strauch plus standard facts on Verma constituents (Humphreys, Chap. 6); (2),(3) from Orlik, ‘On the socle...’, Thm. 1.

items.name: The constituents C(I,s_{i,σ}) indexed by subsets I ⊂ {1,…,n}
items.statement: By Proposition 3.1 (4), for i ∈ {1,…,n-1} and I ⊂ {1,…,n} with #I = i, all C(w,s_{i,σ}) with w({1,…,i}) = I are isomorphic; the common value is denoted C(I,s_{i,σ}), and these are pairwise distinct for distinct (I,s_{i,σ}). One has C(I,s_{i,σ}) ≅ soc (Ind_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)} z^{-s_{i,σ}·λ}w(φ)η)^{Q_p-an} for any such w.
items.note: The (2^n-2)d_K representations C(I,s_{i,σ}) are the ‘extra’ constituents in which the Hodge parameters will be encoded.

items.name: Lemma 3.2: Jacquet–Emerton module and Emerton's induction of the constituents
items.statement: For w with w({1,…,i}) = I: (1) Hom_{T(K)}(z^{-s_{i,σ}·λ}w(φ)ηδ_B, J_B(C(I,s_{i,σ}))) ≅ E, where J_B is the Jacquet–Emerton functor; (2) I_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)}(z^{-s_{i,σ}·λ}w(φ)η) ≅ C(I,s_{i,σ}), where I_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)} is Emerton's induction functor.
items.note: Source issue: the statement and its proof print Hom_{T(Q_p)} where T(K) is meant. The proof uses very strong admissibility (Emerton, Prop. 2.1.2) and Breuil's computation of J_B on such constituents.

items.name: The Jacquet–Emerton functor J_B and Emerton's adjunction
items.statement: Emerton's locally analytic Jacquet functor J_B on essentially admissible locally analytic representations, its universal property, the notion of a balanced map and the resulting adjunction Hom_{T(K)}(δ, J_B(V)) ≅ Hom_{GL_n(K)}(I_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)}δ, V) (Emerton, ‘Jacquet modules II’, Def. 0.8 and Thm. 0.13), together with the closed induction functor I_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)}.
items.note: This adjunction is the bridge used twice in §4 to turn a tangent-space computation on an eigenvariety into an injection of GL_n(K)-representations.

items.name: The subrepresentations PS_1(w(φ),h) and the amalgamation π_1(φ,h)
items.statement: PS_1(w(φ),h) ⊂ PS(w(φ),h) is the unique subrepresentation with socle π_alg(φ,h) and cosocle ⊕_{i,σ} C(w,s_{i,σ}); after fixing isomorphisms π_alg(φ,h) ≅ L(λ) ⊗_E I_sm(w(φ)) for all w, the amalgamated sum ⊕^{w∈S_n}_{π_alg(φ,h)} PS_1(w(φ),h) has a unique quotient π_1(φ,h) with socle π_alg(φ,h); π_1(φ,h) is an extension of ⊕_{i=1,…,n-1, σ∈Σ_K, I⊂{1,…,n}, #I=i} C(I,s_{i,σ}) — that is (2^n-2)d_K constituents — by π_alg(φ,h).
items.note: π_1(φ,h) depends only on (φ,h): it is the same for every D ∈ ΦΓ_nc(φ,h). Everything that distinguishes the D's happens in Ext^1(π_alg(φ,h), π_1(φ,h)).

items.name: Proposition 3.3: self-extensions of π_alg(φ,h) and the maps ζ_w
items.statement: (1) For w ∈ S_n and ψ ∈ Hom_{g'}(T(K),E), I_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)}(w(φ)ηz^λ(1+ψε)) is an extension of π_alg(φ,h) by itself, and ζ_w: Hom_{g'}(T(K),E) → Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg(φ,h),π_alg(φ,h)) is bijective, restricting to Hom_sm(T(K),E) ≅ Ext^1_lalg(π_alg(φ,h),π_alg(φ,h)); hence dim_E Ext^1_lalg = n and dim_E Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg,π_alg) = n + d_K. (2) For w_1,w_2, ζ_{w_2} = ζ_{w_1}∘(w_2w_1^{-1}) on Hom_{g'}(T(K),E).
items.note: Part (2) is proved through the Bernstein centre: the maps J_w: ∏_i Spec H_{w^{-1}(i)} → Spec H of Caraiani–Emerton–Gee–Geraghty–Paškūnas–Shin, Lem. 3.22, satisfy J_{w_2} = (w_2w_1^{-1})∘J_{w_1} and their tangent maps are the ζ_w. Compare Lemma 2.11 on the Galois side.

items.name: The Bernstein centre of the component of π_sm(φ) and its tangent maps
items.statement: H (resp. H_i ≅ G_m) is the Bernstein centre over E attached to the smooth representation π_sm(φ) of GL_n(K) (resp. to φ_i of K^×); for w ∈ S_n there is a natural map J_w: ∏_{i=1}^n Spec H_{w^{-1}(i)} → Spec H sending (φ'_i) to the point of the unramified principal series (Ind_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)}(⊠_i φ'_i)η)^∞, inducing an isomorphism on completions at closed points.
items.note: SR.3 constructs the Bernstein decomposition and centre; SR.1 the Hecke algebras and idempotents e_U it is built from. The specific statement used (Caraiani–Emerton–Gee–Geraghty–Paškūnas–Shin Lem. 3.22, Thm. 4.19) is a completion-level refinement of that stage's output. Source issue: the product in the printed formula is written ⊠^r_{i=1} instead of ⊠^n_{i=1}.

items.name: Schraen's spectral sequence for Ext groups into a principal series
items.statement: For G = Res^K_{Q_p} GL_n and a character δ of T(K) there is a spectral sequence Ext^p_{T(K)}(H_q(N^-(K),V), δ) ⇒ Ext^{p+q}_{GL_n(K)}(V, (Ind_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)}δ)^{Q_p-an}) (Schraen, Cor. 4.9), valid under a separatedness hypothesis verified here for π_alg(φ,h) and its self-extensions.
items.locator: used in Lemma 3.5 and Proposition 3.6, pp. 36–38
items.note: Together with Ext^i_{T(K)}(χ,χ') = 0 for χ ≠ χ' and the classical Jacquet module J_{N^-}(I_sm(φ)) ≅ ⊕_{w'} w'(φ)η, this computes all the Ext^1 groups the paper needs.

items.name: Lemma 3.5: one-dimensionality of the extension groups with a constituent
items.statement: For every C(I,s_{i,σ}): (1) dim_E Ext^1_{GL_n}(C(I,s_{i,σ}),π_alg(φ,h)) = dim_E Ext^1_{GL_n}(π_alg(φ,h),C(I,s_{i,σ})) = 1. (2) For a non-split π̃_alg(φ,h) ∈ Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg(φ,h),π_alg(φ,h)), the pull-back map Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg(φ,h),C(I,s_{i,σ})) → Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π̃_alg(φ,h),C(I,s_{i,σ})) is bijective.
items.note: (1) from Breuil–Qian Prop. 5.1.14 and Lem. 3.2.4 (ii); the paper also gives a proof by Schraen's spectral sequence. (2) is what makes the ‘third layer’ of π_min(D) rigid.

items.name: The maps ζ_w: Hom(T(K),E) → Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg(φ,h), π_1(φ,h))
items.statement: Sending ψ to (Ind_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)} w(φ)ηz^λ(1+ψε))^{Q_p-an}, pulling back along π_alg(φ,h) ↪ PS_1(w(φ),h) and pushing forward along PS_1(w(φ),h) ↪ π_1(φ,h); ζ_w is independent of the chosen isomorphism (3.2), and can equivalently be described through Emerton's functor I_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)}.
items.note: ζ_w is the GL_n(K)-side counterpart of κ_w^{-1}: the two are matched in Theorem 3.21.

items.name: Proposition 3.6: Ext^1(π_alg, PS_1) is exactly Hom(T(K),E)
items.statement: (1) For w ∈ S_n the map (3.10) is bijective, so dim_E Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg(φ,h),PS_1(w(φ),h)) = n + nd_K. (2) ζ_w restricted to Hom_{g'}(T(K),E) is (3.4) followed by the push-forward Ext^1(π_alg,π_alg) ↪ Ext^1(π_alg,π_1(φ,h)).
items.note: n + nd_K = dim Hom(T(K),E): the extensions of π_alg(φ,h) by a single PS_1 are exactly the deformations of the trianguline parameter. Source issue: the proof cites [31, Lem. 2.26] where the same lemma is cited as [32, Lem. 2.26] on pp. 37 and 39.

items.name: Proposition 3.8: the extension group of π_alg(φ,h) by π_1(φ,h)
items.statement: (1) There is an exact sequence 0 → Ext^1(π_alg,π_alg) → Ext^1(π_alg,π_1(φ,h)) → ⊕_{i=1,…,n-1, σ∈Σ_K, #I=i} Ext^1(π_alg,C(I,s_{i,σ})) → 0, so dim_E Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) = n + (2^n-1)d_K. (2) The map t_{φ,h}: ⊕_{w∈S_n} Hom(T(K),E) --(ζ_w)--> Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) is surjective.
items.note: The surjectivity of (3.13) is the GL_n(K)-side counterpart of Proposition 2.12, and the gap between its source (n!·n(1+d_K)) and target is what creates Ker(t_D). Source issue: the direct sum is printed over I ⊂ {1,…,n-1}, which contradicts the dimension n + (2^n-1)d_K stated in the same proposition.

items.name: The amalgamated principal series π(φ,h) and the comparison with π_1(φ,h)
items.statement: π(φ,h) is the unique quotient of ⊕^{w∈S_n}_{π_alg(φ,h)} PS(w(φ),h) with socle π_alg(φ,h) (the representation π(ρ)^{fs} of Breuil–Herzig, Def. 5.7); π_1(φ,h) is the first two layers of its socle filtration, and the push-forward Ext^1(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) ≅ Ext^1(π_alg(φ,h),π(φ,h)) is an isomorphism, so every statement below holds with π_1(φ,h) replaced by π(φ,h).
items.note: This is why Theorem 1.1 of the introduction can be stated with the much larger π(α,h) while all proofs use π_1.

items.name: The subspaces Ext^1_g ⊂ Ext^1_{g'} ⊂ Ext^1_w of Ext^1(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h))
items.statement: Ext^1_g (resp. Ext^1_{g'}, resp. Ext^1_w = Ext^1_{T_w}) is the image of Ext^1_lalg(π_alg,π_alg) (resp. of Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg,π_alg), resp. of ζ_w); ζ_w gives an isomorphism Hom(T(K),E) ≅ Ext^1_w(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)), and for w_1,w_2 the identification of Ext^1_{g'} is compatible with the action of w_2w_1^{-1} on Hom_{g'}(T(K),E).
items.note: The whole comparison of §3.2 is the statement that this filtration matches, subspace by subspace, the filtration Ext^1_0 ⊂ Ext^1_g ⊂ Ext^1_{g'} ⊂ Ext^1_w ⊂ Ext^1 on the Galois side.

items.name: The Levi data (φ_{F_P,i}, h^i) attached to a P-filtration of ⊕φ_i and the parabolic induction (3.19)
items.statement: For a P-filtration F_P of ⊕_{i=1}^n φ_i put φ_{F_P,i} := ⊗ φ_j over the φ_j in gr_i F_P, h^i the corresponding block of h and λ^i the corresponding dominant weight; §3.1.2 applied to (φ_{F_P,i},h^i) gives GL_{n_i}(K)-representations π_alg(φ_{F_P,i},h^i) ⊂ π_1(φ_{F_P,i},h^i). After fixing compatible isomorphisms one gets π_alg(φ,h) ≅ (Ind_{P^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)}(⊠_i π_alg(φ_{F_P,i},h^i))ε^{-1}∘θ^P)^{lalg} ↪ (Ind_{P^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)}(⊗̂_i π_1(φ_{F_P,i},h^i))ε^{-1}∘θ^P)^{Q_p-an}.
items.note: Source issue: the printed formula for the n_i = 1 case is φ_{n_1+…+n_{i-1}} z^{h_{n_1+…+n_{i-1}}}, whose index is an empty sum for i = 1; it must be n_1+…+n_{i-1}+1.

items.name: Lemma 3.10: which constituents C(I,s_{i,σ}) appear in a parabolic induction
items.statement: C(I,s_{i,σ}) (i ∈ {1,…,n-1}, I ⊂ {1,…,n}, #I = i) is a constituent of (Ind_{P^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)}(⊗̂_j π_1(φ_{F_P,j},h^j))ε^{-1}∘θ^P)^{Q_p-an} if and only if either (1) there is k with n_1+…+n_{k-1}+1 ≤ i ≤ n_1+…+n_k-1 and {j : φ_j ∈ Fil_{k-1}} ⊂ I ⊂ {j : φ_j ∈ Fil_k}, or (2) i = n_1+…+n_k for some k ≤ r-1 and I = {j : φ_j ∈ Fil_k}. Each such constituent has multiplicity one and lies in the socle of the quotient by π_alg(φ,h).
items.note: Proved with Orlik–Strauch and the multiplicity-one of L^-(-s_{i,σ}·λ) in the parabolic Verma module U(gl_{n,Σ_K}) ⊗_{U(p_{Σ_K})}(-λ).

items.name: The subrepresentation π_{F_P}(φ,h) and the count #S_{F_P}
items.statement: S_{F_P} is the set of constituents C(I,s_{i,σ}) satisfying Lemma 3.10, with #S_{F_P} = (Σ_{i=1}^r (2^{n_i}-2) + (r-1))d_K; π_{F_P}(φ,h) is the unique subrepresentation of the parabolic induction with socle π_alg(φ,h) and π_{F_P}(φ,h)/π_alg(φ,h) ≅ ⊕_{C∈S_{F_P}} C. For P = B and F_P = T_w one has π_{F_P}(φ,h) ≅ PS_1(w(φ),h), and π_{F_P}(φ,h) ↪ π_1(φ,h).

items.name: Proposition 3.11: the extension group for π_{F_P}
items.statement: dim_E Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg(φ,h),π_{F_P}(φ,h)) = n + d_K r + d_K Σ_{i=1}^r (2^{n_i}-2), and the push-forward Ext^1(π_alg(φ,h),π_{F_P}(φ,h)) ↪ Ext^1(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) is injective; its image is denoted Ext^1_{F_P}(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)).

items.name: The parabolic-induction map ζ_{F_P}
items.statement: Combining the map ∏_i Ext^1_{GL_{n_i}(K)}(π_alg(φ_{F_P,i},h^i),π_1(φ_{F_P,i},h^i)) → Ext^1_{L_P(K)}(⊠_i π_alg(φ_{F_P,i},h^i), ⊗̂_i π_1(φ_{F_P,i},h^i)) with parabolic induction and the pull-back along (3.19) gives ζ_{F_P}: ∏_i Ext^1_{GL_{n_i}(K)}(π_alg(φ_{F_P,i},h^i),π_1(φ_{F_P,i},h^i)) → Ext^1_{F_P}(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)).

items.name: Proposition 3.12: ζ_{F_P} is bijective and compatible with the weight maps
items.statement: (1) ζ_{F_P} is bijective. (2) For w with T_w compatible with F_P, the square relating ∏_i Hom(T(K) ∩ L_{P,i}(K),E) ≅ Hom(T(K),E) to ∏_i Ext^1_{T_{w,i}}(π_alg(φ_{F_P,i},h^i),π_1(φ_{F_P,i},h^i)) ≅ Ext^1_w(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) commutes, the bottom map being induced by ζ_{F_P}.
items.note: This is the GL_n(K)-side of Corollary 2.14: the extension theory is ‘multiplicative along the Levi’, which is what makes the induction in Theorem 3.21 possible.

items.name: Proposition 3.13: the two maximal parabolics amalgamate to π_1(φ,h)
items.statement: For F the filtration ⊕_{i≤n-1}φ_i ⊂ ⊕_i φ_i and G the filtration φ_n ⊂ ⊕_i φ_i, C(I,s_{i,σ}) appears in π_F(φ,h) iff I ⊂ {1,…,n-1} and in π_G(φ,h) iff I = I_1 ∪ {n} with I_1 ⊂ {1,…,n-1}, so π_1(φ,h)/π_alg(φ,h) splits as the direct sum of the two quotients; there are exact sequences 0 → π_alg(φ,h) → π_F(φ,h) ⊕ π_G(φ,h) → π_1(φ,h) → 0 and 0 → Ext^1_{g'}(π_alg,π_1) → Ext^1_F(π_alg,π_1) ⊕ Ext^1_G(π_alg,π_1) → Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg,π_1) → 0.
items.note: The exact counterpart of Corollary 2.33 on the Galois side; the two exact sequences are what Theorem 3.21 compares. Source issue: the two parabolic inductions are printed with P_1 and P_2 in place of P_{n-1} and P_1.

items.name: Locally σ-analytic and g_{Σ_K∖{σ}}-algebraic representations
items.statement: A locally Q_p-analytic representation V of GL_n(K) is locally σ-analytic when the derived gl_n(K) ⊗_{Q_p} E-action factors through gl_n(K) ⊗_{K,σ} E, and g_{Σ_K∖{σ}}-algebraic when U(g_{Σ_K∖{σ}})v is finite dimensional algebraic for every v ∈ V; Ext^1_σ(V,W) ⊂ Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(V,W) is the subspace of g_{Σ_K∖{σ}}-algebraic extensions, and Hom_{σ,g'}(T(K),E) := Hom_{g'} ∩ Hom_σ.
items.note: This is the GL_n(K)-side of the ‘Σ_K∖{σ}-de Rham’ condition of §2.3.2; the two are matched by t_D.

items.name: The maximal g_{Σ_K∖{σ}}-algebraic subrepresentations π_{1,σ}(φ,h) and PS_{1,σ}(w(φ),h)
items.statement: π_{1,σ}(φ,h) ⊂ π_1(φ,h) is the extension of ⊕_{i,#I=i} C(I,s_{i,σ}) (fixed σ) by π_alg(φ,h); PS_{1,σ}(w(φ),h) = PS_1(w(φ),h) ∩ ((Ind_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)}w(φ)ηz^{λ_σ})^{σ-an} ⊗_E L(λ^σ)). π_{1,σ}(φ,h) is the unique quotient of ⊕^{w}_{π_alg(φ,h)} PS_{1,σ}(w(φ),h) with socle π_alg(φ,h), and is the maximal g_{Σ_K∖{σ}}-algebraic subrepresentation of π_1(φ,h).
items.note: Source issues: the sentence prints π_alg(φ,λ) for π_alg(φ,h), and the displayed embedding has exponent z^{s_{i,σ}·λ_σ} with the minus sign lost and an undefined L^-_σ.

items.name: Lemma 3.15: σ-analytic self-extensions of π_alg(φ,h)
items.statement: dim_E Ext^1_σ(π_alg(φ,h),π_alg(φ,h)) = n + 1, and (3.4) induces an isomorphism Hom_{σ,g'}(T(K),E) ≅ Ext^1_σ(π_alg(φ,h),π_alg(φ,h)).

items.name: Proposition 3.16: Ext^1_σ(π_alg, PS_{1,σ}) ≅ Hom_σ(T(K),E)
items.statement: For w ∈ S_n, the map (3.10) induces an isomorphism Hom_σ(T(K),E) ≅ Ext^1_σ(π_alg(φ,h), PS_{1,σ}(w(φ),h)) (both of dimension 2n). Moreover the connecting map onto ⊕_{i=1}^{n-1} Ext^1_σ(π_alg,C(w,s_{i,σ})) is surjective and Ext^1_σ(π_alg,C(w,s_{i,σ})) ≅ Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg,C(w,s_{i,σ})).

items.name: Proposition 3.18: the σ-part of Ext^1(π_alg,π_1) and the decomposition over Σ_K
items.statement: (1) There is an exact sequence 0 → Ext^1_σ(π_alg,π_alg) → Ext^1_σ(π_alg,π_1(φ,h)) → ⊕_{i,#I=i} Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg,C(I,s_{i,σ})) → 0 and dim_E Ext^1_σ(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) = n + 2^n - 1. (2) t_{φ,h} restricts to a surjection ⊕_{w∈S_n} Hom_σ(T(K),E) ↠ Ext^1_σ(π_alg,π_1). (3) ⊕_{τ∈Σ_K} Ext^1_τ(π_alg,π_1) → Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg,π_1) is surjective and induces an isomorphism ⊕_τ (Ext^1_τ/Ext^1_g) ≅ Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}/Ext^1_g, both sides of dimension (2^n-1)d_K.
items.note: Part (3) is the representation-theoretic reason why the Hodge parameters split up into the family {D_σ}_{σ∈Σ_K}. Source issue: the direct sum in (1) is again printed over I ⊂ {1,…,n-1}.

items.name: Proposition 3.19: the σ-analytic theory is compatible with parabolic induction
items.statement: With π_{F_P,σ}(φ,h) := π_{F_P}(φ,h) ∩ π_{1,σ}(φ,h): (1) dim_E Ext^1_{σ,F_P}(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) = n + r + Σ_{i=1}^r (2^{n_i}-2); (2) ζ_{F_P} induces an isomorphism ∏_i Ext^1_σ(π_alg(φ_{F_P,i},h^i),π_1(φ_{F_P,i},h^i)) ≅ Ext^1_{σ,F_P}(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)), compatibly with the weight maps for any T_w compatible with F_P.

items.name: Proposition 3.20: the σ-analytic F/G amalgamation
items.statement: There is an exact sequence 0 → π_alg(φ,h) → π_{F,σ}(φ,h) ⊕ π_{G,σ}(φ,h) → π_{1,σ}(φ,h) → 0 and consequently 0 → Ext^1_{σ,g'}(π_alg,π_1) → Ext^1_{σ,F}(π_alg,π_1) ⊕ Ext^1_{σ,G}(π_alg,π_1) → Ext^1_σ(π_alg,π_1) → 0.

items.name: The composite (3.41) comparing trianguline deformations with GL_n(K)-extensions
items.statement: The composition ⊕_{w∈S_n} \bar{Ext}^1_w(D,D) --(κ_w)--> ⊕_{w∈S_n} Hom(T(K),E) --t_{φ,h}--> Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)), the first map an isomorphism by (2.14) and the second surjective by Proposition 3.8 (2).
items.note: The left-hand side depends on D, the right-hand side only on (φ,h); Theorem 3.21 says the Galois amalgamation factors through the representation-theoretic one.

items.name: Theorem 3.21: the map t_D
items.statement: The natural surjection ⊕_{w∈S_n} \bar{Ext}^1_w(D,D) ↠ \bar{Ext}^1(D,D) factors through (3.41): there is a unique map t_D: Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) ↠ \bar{Ext}^1(D,D) such that the amalgamation equals t_D composed with (3.41).
items.note: The central theorem of the paper (Theorem 1.3 of the introduction). Proved by induction on n: the F- and G-filtrations give t_{F,D} and t_{G,D} from the rank n-1 case by Proposition 3.12 and Corollary 2.14, they agree on Ext^1_{g'} by Lemma 2.11 and (3.18), and Proposition 3.13 glues them. For the refinements w with 1 < w(n) < n one moves to w_jw ∈ S_{n-1} ∪ S'_{n-1} by Corollary 2.15 (2) and (3.40).

items.name: The two subsets S_{n-1}, S'_{n-1} of S_n used in the induction
items.statement: S_{n-1} = {w : w(n) = n} is the set of refinements compatible with F, and S'_{n-1} := {w ∈ S_n : w(n) = 1}, of cardinality (n-1)!, the set compatible with G.

items.name: The spanning of Hom(T(K),E) by the centres of the maximal Levis
items.statement: Hom(T(K),E) is spanned by the subspaces Hom(Z_j(K),E), j = 1,…,n-1, pulled back along T → Z_{L_j}, together with Hom(Z(K),E), where Z_j is the centre of the Levi L_j of the maximal parabolic P_j; and κ_w^{-1}(Hom(Z_j(K),E)) ⊂ \bar{Ext}^1_{F_{P_j},g'}(D,D).
items.note: Source issue: (3.43) is printed as a direct-sum DECOMPOSITION Hom(T(K),E) = ⊕_j Hom(Z_j(K),E) ⊕ Hom(Z(K),E), which is false for n ≥ 3 on dimension grounds (2(n-1)+1 factors of dimension 1+d_K against n(1+d_K)); only the spanning, which the proof itself states at the end, is needed and true.

items.name: Remark 3.22: the dimension of Ker(t_D)
items.statement: dim_E Ker(t_D) = (2^n - n(n+1)/2 - 1)d_K, and the same t_D works with π_1(φ,h) replaced by π(φ,h) under the isomorphism (3.16).
items.note: From dim Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg,π_1) = n + (2^n-1)d_K and dim \bar{Ext}^1(D,D) = n + (n(n+1)/2)d_K. For n = 2 the kernel vanishes, which is why no new parameter appears for GL_2; for n = 3 it is d_K-dimensional.

items.name: Lemma 3.23: the kernel meets no trianguline direction
items.statement: For every w ∈ S_n, Ker(t_D) ∩ Ext^1_w(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) = 0.
items.note: Immediate from Theorem 3.21 since κ_w and ζ_w are isomorphisms; it is what makes π_min(D) have the same socle filtration shape as π_1(φ,h).

items.name: The representations π_min(D) and π_fs(D)
items.statement: π_min(D) (resp. π_fs(D)) is the extension of Ker(t_D) ⊗_E π_alg(φ,h) ≅ π_alg(φ,h)^{⊕(2^n-n(n+1)/2-1)d_K} by π_1(φ,h) (resp. by π(φ,h)) attached to the subspace Ker(t_D); since End(π(φ,h)) ≅ End(π_1(φ,h)) ≅ End(π_alg(φ,h)) ≅ E, either of them determines Ker(t_D), and π_fs(D) ≅ π_min(D) ⊕_{π_1(φ,h)} π(φ,h).
items.note: π_min(D) is the representation called π_1(D) in the introduction, cut down to the first two layers of π(φ,h); it is the object that encodes the p-adic Hodge parameters.

items.name: The surjection f_D and the induced filtration on Ext^1(π_alg,π_min(D))
items.statement: The exact sequence 0 → Hom(π_alg(φ,h), Ker(t_D) ⊗_E π_alg(φ,h)) → Ext^1(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) --f_D--> Ext^1(π_alg(φ,h),π_min(D)) has f_D surjective (Lemma 3.5 (2)); Ext^1_{F_P}(π_alg,π_min(D)) and Ext^1_g(π_alg,π_min(D)) denote the images of the corresponding subspaces.

items.name: Corollary 3.24: t_D is an isomorphism on each trianguline piece
items.statement: t_D induces isomorphisms Ext^1_g(π_alg(φ,h),π_min(D)) ≅ \bar{Ext}^1_g(D,D) and Ext^1_w(π_alg(φ,h),π_min(D)) ≅ \bar{Ext}^1_w(D,D) for every w ∈ S_n.

items.name: Corollary 3.25: the characterisation of π_min(D)
items.statement: π_min(D) is the unique extension of π_alg(φ,h)^{⊕(2^n-n(n+1)/2-1)d_K} by π_1(φ,h) such that (1) soc π_min(D) ≅ π_alg(φ,h) and soc(π_min(D)/π_alg(φ,h)) ≅ soc(π_1(φ,h)/π_alg(φ,h)); and (2) there is a bijection t_D: Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg(φ,h),π_min(D)) ≅ \bar{Ext}^1(D,D) compatible with trianguline deformations, i.e. for each w the composite Hom(T(K),E) --ζ_w--> Ext^1_w(π_alg,π_min(D)) --t_D--> \bar{Ext}^1(D,D) equals κ_w^{-1} followed by the inclusion.
items.note: This is Corollary 1.5 of the introduction: after passing to π_min(D) the map t_D becomes a bijection, so π_min(D) ‘is’ the deformation space \bar{Ext}^1(D,D) seen from GL_n(K).

items.name: The central character χ_D and the determinant of D
items.note: Source issue: |λ| is printed as the sum over BOTH i and σ, whereas z^k requires k ∈ Z^{Σ_K}; with the printed reading the displayed formula for ∧^n D fails for K ≠ Q_p.

items.name: Proposition 3.26: central and infinitesimal characters of π_min(D)
items.statement: π_min(D) has central character χ_D and infinitesimal character ξ_λ.
items.note: Proved by comparing two tangent maps: d_Sen on \bar{Ext}^1(D,D), reading the Sen weights of a deformation, and d_inf on Ext^1(π_alg,π_1), reading the action of the centre Z_K of U(gl_{n,Σ_K}); the Harish-Chandra isomorphism intertwines them, so the square with t_D commutes.

items.name: Proposition 3.27: t_D is compatible with parabolic induction
items.statement: t_D restricts to a surjection t_{D,F_P}: Ext^1_{F_P}(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) ↠ \bar{Ext}^1_{F_P}(D,D), the square relating ∏_i t_{M_i} through ζ_{F_P} (3.26) and κ_{F_P} (2.19) commutes, and consequently ⊕_{i=1}^r Ker(t_{M_i}) ≅ Ker(t_{D,F_P}) = Ker(t_D) ∩ Ext^1_{F_P}(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)).
items.note: The parameters are therefore ‘additive along a parabolic’: the Hodge parameters of D visible through F_P are exactly those of its graded pieces.

items.name: π_{min,F_P}(D) and its description by Emerton's induction
items.statement: π_{min,F_P}(D) ⊂ π_min(D) is the extension of Ker(t_{D,F_P}) ⊗_E π_alg(φ,h) ≅ π_alg(φ,h)^{⊕Σ_i d_K(2^{n_i}-n_i(n_i+1)/2-1)} by π_1(φ,h); it is the maximal subrepresentation of π_min(D) coming from extensions of π_alg(φ,h) by π_{F_P}(φ,h), and I_{P^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)}((⊗̂_i π_min(M_i)) ⊗_E ε^{-1}∘θ^P) ↪ π_{min,F_P}(D).

items.name: Corollary 3.29: the σ-part t_{D,σ} and its parabolic compatibility
items.statement: (1) The surjection (2.24) factors through (3.41) restricted to the σ-parts and the restriction t_{D,σ}: Ext^1_σ(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) ↠ \bar{Ext}^1_σ(D,D). (2) For a P-filtration F_P the analogous square commutes and ⊕_{i=1}^r Ker t_{M_i,σ} ≅ Ker t_{D,F_P,σ}.

items.name: Remark 3.30: dimensions in the σ-theory and π_min(D)_σ
items.statement: dim_E \bar{Ext}^1_σ(D,D) = n + n(n+1)/2 and dim_E Ker(t_{D,σ}) = 2^n - n(n+1)/2 - 1; Ker(t_{D,σ}) = Ker(t_D) ∩ Ext^1_σ(π_alg,π_1), and π_min(D)_σ, the extension of Ker(t_{D,σ}) ⊗_E π_alg(φ,h) by π_{1,σ}(φ,h), is the maximal g_{Σ_K∖{σ}}-algebraic subrepresentation of π_min(D).

items.name: Corollary 3.31: π_min(D) is the amalgam of its σ-parts
items.statement: ⊕_{σ∈Σ_K} Ker(t_{D,σ}) ≅ Ker(t_D), and consequently π_min(D) ≅ ⊕^{σ∈Σ_K}_{π_alg(φ,h)} π_min(D)_σ.
items.note: Proved from Proposition 3.18 (3) plus Lemma 3.23 and a dimension count; this is the representation-theoretic counterpart of the fact that only the family {D_σ} is seen.

items.name: Corollaries 3.32–3.33: t_{D_σ} and the identification with deformations of D_σ
items.statement: t_{D_σ} := 𝔗_σ ∘ t_{D,σ}: Ext^1_σ(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) ↠ \bar{Ext}^1_σ(D,D) ≅ \bar{Ext}^1_σ(D_σ,D_σ) has Ker t_{D_σ} = Ker t_{D,σ}, depends only on D_σ, is compatible with parabolic induction — ⊕_i Ker t_{M_{i,σ}} ≅ Ker t_{D_σ,F_P} — and induces an isomorphism t_{D_σ}: Ext^1_σ(π_alg(φ,h),π_min(D)_σ) ≅ \bar{Ext}^1_σ(D_σ,D_σ).

items.name: Theorem 3.34: π_min(D) determines the family {D_σ}
items.statement: For D,D' ∈ ΦΓ_nc(φ,h) and σ ∈ Σ_K, π_min(D)_σ ≅ π_min(D')_σ if and only if D_σ ≅ D'_σ; consequently π_min(D) ≅ π_min(D') if and only if D_σ ≅ D'_σ for all σ ∈ Σ_K. In particular, for K = Q_p, π_min(D) determines D.
items.note: The main local theorem (Theorem 1.1 (1) of the introduction). The ‘if’ direction is an induction on n: Corollary 3.32 (2) and (3.51) give D_{1,σ} ≅ D'_{1,σ} and C_{1,σ} ≅ C'_{1,σ}, and then the higher-intertwining subspace L of §2.4 is computed on the GL_n(K)-side as the kernel of an amalgamation of Ext groups and identified with L(D_σ,D_{1,σ},C_{1,σ}), which determines D_σ by Corollary 2.38 (1). Source issue: the sentence deducing the second isomorphism repeats L(D_σ,…) where L(D'_σ,…) is meant.

items.name: The deformation rings R_D, R_{D,w}, R_{D,g}, R_δ and their tangent spaces
items.statement: R_D is the universal deformation ring of D over local Artinian E-algebras (End(D) ≅ E), R_{D,w} that of T_w-deformations, R_{D,g} that of de Rham (equivalently crystabelline) deformations, and R_δ (resp. R_{δ,g}) that of a continuous character δ of T(K) (resp. of its locally algebraic deformations). All are formally smooth complete local Noetherian E-algebras by genericity, with tangent spaces Ext^1_*(D,D), Hom(T(K),E) and Hom_sm(T(K),E).
items.note: R08.1 proves framed local representability and the tangent/obstruction description for Galois deformation rings; the (φ,Γ)-module analogues used here, with their trianguline and de Rham variants, are the objects Bellaïche–Chenevier §2.3.5, §2.5.3 and Nakamura §2 construct.

items.name: The Cartesian square (3.55) and the algebras A_0, A_D, A_{D,w}
items.statement: κ_w induces a Cartesian square of Artinian E-algebras relating R_{w(φ)z^h}/m², R_{w(φ)z^h,g}/m², R_{D,w}/m² and R_{D,g}/m². With H the Bernstein centre and Ĥ_φ its completion at π_sm(φ), the composite A_0 := Ĥ_φ/m² ≅ R_{w(φ)z^h,g}/m² ↪ R_{D,g}/m² is independent of w (Lemma 2.11 and Proposition 3.3 (2)); one sets A_D := R_D/m² ×_{R_{D,g}/m²} A_0 and A_{D,w} := R_{D,w}/m² ×_{R_{D,g}/m²} A_0 ≅ R_{w(φ)z^h}/m², with tangent spaces \bar{Ext}^1(D,D) and \bar{Ext}^1_w(D,D) ≅ Hom(T(K),E), and I_w := Ker(A_D ↠ A_{D,w}); A_D ↪ ∏_w A_{D,w}.
items.note: A_D is the ring-theoretic incarnation of \bar{Ext}^1(D,D): the quotient of R_D/m² cut out by trivialising the smooth part of the parameter.

items.name: The universal extensions π_1(φ,h)^univ, π_1(φ,h)^univ_w and δ̃_w^univ
items.statement: π_1(φ,h)^univ (resp. π_1(φ,h)^univ_w) is the tautological extension of Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) ⊗_E π_alg(φ,h) (resp. of Ext^1_w(…) ⊗_E π_alg(φ,h)) by π_1(φ,h); δ_w := w(φ)z^h(ε^{-1}∘θ) and δ̃_w^univ is the tautological extension of Ext^1_{T(K)}(δ_w,δ_w) ⊗_E δ_w ≅ Hom(T(K),E) ⊗_E δ_w by δ_w, carrying a natural A_{D,w} ≅ R_{w(φ)z^h}/m²-action.
items.note: The T(K)-action and the A_{D,w}-action on δ̃_w^univ determine each other, because E[T(K)] → R_{δ_w}/m² is surjective; this is the pivot of the local–global argument.

items.name: Lemma 3.35: Emerton's induction of δ̃_w^univ is the universal extension
items.statement: I_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)} δ̃_w^univ is the universal extension of π_alg(φ,h) ⊗_E Ext^1_{GL_n(K)}(π_alg(φ,h),PS_1(w(φ),h)) by PS_1(w(φ),h); hence I_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)} δ̃_w^univ ⊕_{PS_1(w(φ),h)} π_1(φ,h) ≅ π_1(φ,h)^univ_w.

items.name: Theorem 3.36: the A_D-action on the universal extension
items.statement: There is a unique A_D-action on π_1(φ,h)^univ such that for every w ∈ S_n there is an A_{D,w} × GL_n(K)-equivariant injection π_1(φ,h)^univ_w ↪ π_1(φ,h)^univ[I_w].
items.note: A reformulation of Theorem 3.21 (Corollary 1.6 of the introduction): the Hodge parameter of D is encoded in an action of the Artinian ring A_D on a representation that does not depend on D. Source issue: the composition defining the action is printed as landing in π_1(φ,h)^univ_w instead of π_1(φ,h)^univ.

items.name: Corollary 3.37: π_min(D) as the m_{A_D}-torsion of the universal extension
items.statement: π_min(D) ≅ π_1(φ,h)^univ[m_{A_D}].
items.note: This is what makes the local–global compatibility argument possible: one produces an A_D-equivariant injection of π_1(φ,h)^univ into a patched Banach representation and then takes m_{A_D}-torsion.

items.name: The patched module M_∞, the Banach representation Π_∞ and the ring R_∞
items.statement: M_∞ is the patched module of Caraiani–Emerton–Gee–Geraghty–Paškūnas–Shin §2; Π_∞ := Hom^cont_{O_E}(M_∞,E) with the maximum norm is a unitary Banach representation of GL_n(K) carrying an action of the patched deformation ring R_∞ ≅ R^□_{ρ̄} ⊗̂_{O_E} R^℘_∞, where ρ̄ is the local residual representation at the chosen place.
items.note: R31.5 constructs the patched completed module with its finiteness, projectivity and support properties; that is exactly the input this section consumes. Everything the paper adds happens on top of it.

items.name: The patched eigenvariety E, the sheaf M and their characterisation
items.statement: E ↪ (Spf R^□_{ρ̄})^rig × T̂ × (Spf R^℘_∞)^rig is the patched eigenvariety, with a coherent sheaf M such that Γ(E,M)^∨ ≅ J_B(Π_∞^{R_∞-an}) T(K) × R_∞-equivariantly; a point x = (ρ_{x,℘}, δ_x, m^℘_x) lies on E if and only if Hom_{T(K)}(δ_x, J_B(Π_∞^{R_∞-an})[m_x]) ≠ 0.
items.note: Constructed as in Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen; the variant used here is Ding's [32, §4.1.2]. PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 routes the patched eigenvariety and its components to the same stage.

items.name: The trianguline variety X^□_tri(ρ̄), the twist ι_p and the embedding of E
items.statement: X^□_tri(ρ̄) ↪ (Spf R^□_{ρ̄})^rig × T̂ is the trianguline variety of Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen §2.2, ι_p(ρ_p,χ) = (ρ_p, χδ_B(ε^{-1}∘θ)) the twisting map, and (4.1) factors through E ↪ ι_p(X^□_tri(ρ̄)) × (Spf R^℘_∞)^rig, identifying E with a union of irreducible components; dim X^□_tri(ρ̄) = n² + d_K n(n+1)/2, the n² coming from the framing.
items.note: PAPER-BREUIL-HELLMANN-SCHRAEN-19 proposes the roadmap that constructs X_tri and proves its smoothness at non-critical points; the present paper consumes exactly those two statements (its Thm. 2.6 (iii)).

items.name: Lemma 4.1: no companion points of non-dominant weight
items.statement: Let ρ be a continuous representation with residual reduction ρ̄ and D := D_rig(ρ) ∈ ΦΓ_nc(φ,h). For a continuous character δ of T(K), (ρ,δ) ∈ X^□_tri(ρ̄) if and only if δ = w(φ)z^h for some w ∈ S_n.
items.note: The ‘only if’ uses that a non-critical D has no companion points of non-dominant weight (Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen Thm. 4.2.3; Breuil–Ding Cor. 6.4.12). This is what makes the finitely many points x_w the whole fibre and gives the vanishing Hom(C(I,s_{i,σ}), Π_∞[a_x]) = 0.

items.name: Smoothness of E at the points x_w and local freeness of M
items.statement: Assume there is a maximal ideal m^℘ of R^℘_∞[1/p] with Π_∞[m_x]^lalg ≠ 0 for m_x = (m_ρ,m^℘); then Π_∞[m_x]^lalg ≅ π_alg(φ,h), the points x_w = (ρ, δ_wδ_B, m^℘) lie on E for all w ∈ S_n and are all the points of E above m_x, X^□_tri(ρ̄) is smooth at ι_p^{-1}(x_{w,℘}), (4.2) is a local isomorphism at x_w, E is smooth at every x_w, and M is locally free of rank one there.
items.note: Source issue: the identification Π_∞[m_x]^lalg ≅ π_alg(φ,h) is cited as [23, Thm. 4.35] on p. 60 and as [23, Thm. 4.3.5] on p. 61.

items.name: The framed deformation rings R^□_D, R^□_{D,w}, R^□_{D,g} and the ideal a
items.statement: R^□_D := R_D ⊗_{R_ρ} R^□_ρ ≅ R^□_ρ, and similarly R^□_{D,w}, R^□_{D,g}; there are Cartesian diagrams relating A_D, A_{D,w}, A_0 to them. One chooses an ideal a ⊃ m²_{R^□_D} with a/m² ⊕ m_{A_D}/m² ≅ m_{R^□_D}/m², so that A_D ≅ R^□_D/a, A_{D,w} ≅ R^□_{D,w}/a and A_0 ≅ R^□_{D,g}/a; a is also viewed in R^□_{ρ̄}[1/p] and a_x := (a, m^℘) ⊂ R_∞[1/p].
items.note: The ideal a is the device that separates the framing directions (which the GL_n(K)-side cannot see) from the parameters that A_D records.

items.name: Lemma 4.2: the a_x-torsion and its locally algebraic vectors
items.note: Part (2) is the multiplicity-one statement that makes the universal extension embed at most once; it is proved from the Bernstein-centre description of the R_∞-action on locally algebraic vectors (Caraiani–Emerton–Gee–Geraghty–Paškūnas–Shin Lem. 4.17, Thm. 4.19).

items.name: The tangent-level fibre M_{x̃_w} and its identification with δ̃_w^univ δ_B
items.statement: For a smooth affinoid neighbourhood U of x_w containing no other x_{w'}, M_{x̃_w} := M(U)/(a + m^℘) is a T(K) × R_∞-module with M_{x̃_w}^∨ ↪ J_B(Π_∞^{R_∞-an}[a_x]); since D is non-critical the completion of X^□_tri(ρ̄) at ι_p^{-1}(x_{w,℘}) is R^□_{D,w}, so M_{x̃_w} ≅ R^□_{D,w}/a of dimension 1 + n + nd_K, and there is a T(K) × A_{D,w}-equivariant isomorphism M_{x̃_w}^∨ ≅ δ̃_w^univ δ_B, the T(K)-action being that of (4.5).
items.note: This is the heart of the local–global argument: the tangent space of the eigenvariety at a companion point IS the universal deformation of the trianguline parameter.

items.name: Lemma 4.3: the balanced map and the injection ι_w
items.statement: The map (4.4) is balanced in Emerton's sense, hence induces a GL_n(K) × R_∞-equivariant injection ι_w: I_{B^-(K)}^{GL_n(K)} δ̃_w^univ ↪ Π_∞^{R_∞-an}[a_x], with the R_∞-action factoring through A_{D,w}.

items.name: Lemma 4.4: the m_x-torsion of the image is exactly PS_1(w(φ),h)
items.statement: (Im ι_w)[m_x] ≅ PS_1(w(φ),h).
items.note: Proved using Lemma 4.1 and Lemma 3.2 (1) to kill the other constituents, plus the semisimplicity statement J_B(Π_∞[m_x])[T(K)=δ_wδ_B] ≅ J_B(Π_∞[m_x]){T(K)=δ_wδ_B}, itself deduced from the global triangulation theory (Bergdall, Thm. 5.3) and local freeness of M.

items.name: Theorem 4.5: the universal extension embeds in the patched representation
items.statement: Let π̃ be the closed subrepresentation of Π_∞^{R_∞-an}[a_x] generated by Im ι_w for all w ∈ S_n. Then there is a GL_n(K) × A_D-equivariant isomorphism π_1(φ,h)^univ ≅ π̃, for the A_D-action of Theorem 3.36.
items.note: The global input is used only through: multiplicity one (Lemma 4.2 (2)), the vanishing of Hom from the constituents (Lemma 4.1 + Lemma 3.2), and the tangent computation (4.4). The A_D-equivariance is then forced by Theorem 3.36.

items.name: Corollary 4.6: π_min(D) embeds in Π_∞[m_x]
items.note: Source issue: the printed chain has Π_∞^{R_∞-an}[a_x][m_D] with an undefined m_D; Lemma 4.2 (1) shows it is m_{A_D}. Remark 4.7 extends the injection to π_fs(D) using Breuil–Herzig Thm. 5.12.

items.name: Corollary 4.8: π_min(D) is the maximal such subrepresentation
items.statement: π_min(D) is the maximal subrepresentation of Π_∞^{R_∞-an}[m_x] given by extensions of π_alg(φ,h) by π_1(φ,h).
items.note: Source issue: the proof calls π̃ ‘the universal extension of π_1(φ,h) by π_alg(φ,h)’, with sub and quotient interchanged relative to the paper's own convention and to the statement being proved.

items.name: Corollary 4.9: Π_∞[m_x] determines the Hodge parameters
items.statement: Π_∞^{R_∞-an}[m_x] determines the family {D_σ}_{σ∈Σ_K} for D = D_rig(ρ); in particular, when K = Q_p it determines ρ.
items.note: Combines Corollary 4.8 with Theorem 3.34; that D is non-critical is itself readable off Π_∞[m_x] by Breuil–Hellmann–Schraen Thm. 5.3.3 (crystalline case) and Breuil–Ding Thm. 1.3 (crystabelline non-crystalline case).

items.name: Hypothesis 4.10 on a subspace Ext^1_U(D,D)
items.statement: For a subspace Ext^1_U(D,D) ⊂ Ext^1(D,D), with Ext^1_{U,w}(D,D) := Ext^1_U(D,D) ∩ Ext^1_w(D,D), the hypotheses are: (1) Ext^1_U(D,D) ∩ Ext^1_g(D,D) = 0; (2) dim_E Ext^1_{U,w}(D,D) = nd_K for every w ∈ S_n.
items.note: These are the properties that the image of a global (polarised, partially de Rham away from ℘) deformation space has, once the adjoint Selmer group vanishes; the point of §4.2.1 is that they suffice.

items.name: Corollary 4.11: Ext^1_U is a complement of Ext^1_g
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 4.10, ⊕_{w∈S_n} Ext^1_{U,w}(D,D) → Ext^1_U(D,D) is surjective and dim_E Ext^1_U(D,D) = (n(n+1)/2)d_K, i.e. Ext^1_U(D,D) ≅ Ext^1(D,D)/Ext^1_g(D,D).

items.name: Corollary 4.12: the restricted map t_{D,U} has the same kernel as t_D
items.statement: With Ext^1_{U,w}(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) the image of Ext^1_{U,w}(D,D) under ζ_w∘κ_w and Ext^1_U(π_alg,π_1) the subspace they generate: (1) t_{φ,h} factors through a surjection t_{D,U}: Ext^1_U(π_alg(φ,h),π_1(φ,h)) ↠ Ext^1_U(D,D); (2) Ker t_{D,U} ≅ Ker t_D.
items.note: So the whole of Ker(t_D) — all the Hodge parameters — is already visible inside the much smaller space cut out by a global deformation condition. Source issue: the direct sum in (4.11) is again indexed by I ⊂ {1,…,n-1}.

items.name: π_1(φ,h)^univ_U, the rings A_{D,U}, A_{D,U,w}, A_{U,w} and δ̃^univ_{U,w}
items.statement: π_1(φ,h)^univ_U (resp. π_1(φ,h)^univ_{U,w}) is the tautological extension of Ext^1_U(π_alg,π_1) ⊗_E π_alg (resp. Ext^1_{U,w}(π_alg,π_1) ⊗_E π_alg) by π_1(φ,h); A_{D,U} (resp. A_{D,U,w}) is the quotient of R_D/m² (resp. R_{D,w}/m²) attached to Ext^1_U(D,D) (resp. Ext^1_{U,w}(D,D)), A_{U,w} the corresponding quotient of R_{w(φ)z^h}/m², with κ_w: A_{U,w} ≅ A_{D,U,w}, and δ̃^univ_{U,w} := A_{U,w}^∨ the tautological extension of Ext^1_U(δ_w,δ_w) ⊗_E δ_w by δ_w; the T(K)- and A_{U,w}-actions on it determine each other.

items.name: Corollary 4.13: the A_{D,U}-action and π_min(D)
items.statement: (1) There is a unique A_{D,U}-action on π_1(φ,h)^univ_U such that for every w there is a GL_n(K) × A_{D,U,w}-equivariant injection π_1(φ,h)^univ_{U,w} ↪ π_1(φ,h)^univ_U[I_w]; (2) π_1(φ,h)^univ_U[m_{A_{D,U}}] ≅ π_min(D).

items.name: The definite unitary group, the tame level and the spaces of p-adic automorphic forms
items.statement: F/F^+ is a CM extension, G/F^+ a unitary group with G ×_{F^+} F ≅ GL_n and G(F^+ ⊗_Q R) compact, every place of F^+ above p split in F, ℘ a fixed place above p with K := F^+_℘ ≅ F_{℘̃}; for v ∈ S_p∖{℘} a dominant weight ξ_v and an inertial type τ_v give σ(τ_v) ⊗_E L(ξ_v) and a lattice W_{ξ,τ}. For a sufficiently small tame level U^℘ one forms S_{ξ,τ}(U^℘U_℘, O_E/ϖ^k) of functions on G(F^+)∖G(A^∞_{F^+}) transforming under U^℘U_℘, and Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E) := (lim_k lim_{U_℘} S_{ξ,τ})⊗_{O_E}E, an admissible unitary Banach representation of GL_n(K).
items.note: AF.5 identifies algebraic modular forms on groups compact at infinity with functions on finite adelic double cosets valued in an algebraic representation; the completed version Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E) is the p-adic limit of exactly those spaces. Source issue: W_{ξ,τ} is printed as a lattice in a single σ(τ_v) ⊗ L(ξ_v) although it is acted on by ∏_{v∈S_p∖{℘}} U_v and must be a lattice in the tensor product over those v.

items.name: The Hecke algebra T(U^℘) and the maximal ideal m_ρ attached to ρ
items.statement: T(U^℘) is the polynomial O_E-algebra on the operators T^{(j)}_{ṽ} = [U_v ι_ṽ^{-1} diag(1_{n-j}, ϖ_ṽ 1_j) U_v] for v ∉ S split in F and j = 1,…,n, acting on Ŝ_{ξ,τ}(U^℘,E) commuting with GL_n(K). To a continuous ρ: Gal_{F,S} → GL_n(E) with ρ^c ≅ ρ^∨ ⊗_E ε^{1-n} is attached the maximal ideal m_ρ generated by the (-1)^j(#k_ṽ)^{j(j-1)/2}T^{(j)}_{ṽ} - a^{(j)}_{ṽ}, where the a^{(j)}_{ṽ} are the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of ρ(Frob_ṽ).
items.note: SR.1 builds the Hecke algebras and their double-coset operators; AF.5 the dictionary with automorphic forms. The normalisation with the signs and the powers of #k_ṽ is the one that makes m_ρ match the Galois side.

items.name: The eigenvariety E(U^℘), its sheaf M(U^℘), and classical and generic points
